items.summary: Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft's new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game "just-in-time" shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes. Microsoft's Advanced Shade
items.content:
Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology is now part of Nvidia’s drivers.

Nvidia is rolling out a new GPU driver today (621.01) that enables Microsoft’s new Advanced Shader Delivery technology to speed up game launches. The technology also removes mid-game “just-in-time” shader compilation, reducing stuttering and CPU spikes.

Microsoft’s Advanced Shader Delivery works by offloading shader compilation for different hardware combinations to the cloud. “Using DirectX 12, Windows 11, and the Microsoft Agility SDK, developers capture shaders into a State Object Database (SODB), allowing Microsoft’s cloud network to precompile shaders for hundreds of thousands of hardware and driver combinations,” explains Nvidia’s Andrew Burnes .

Gears of War: E-Day and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 now both support Advanced Shader Delivery, as long as you download the games via the Xbox PC app. “This system is storefront-agnostic, meaning you benefit even when playing games purchased on Steam, as long as the Xbox PC app is installed on your PC,” says Burnes.

Advanced Shader Delivery will let you skip the annoying shader compilation screen in Call of Duty , and it should improve the overall performance of supported games. “With a near-100 percent cache hit rate, it eliminates mid-game ‘just-in-time’ shader compilation, wiping out CPU spikes and frame stutters in titles like Gears of War: E-Day , and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 .

You can download Nvidia’s latest 621.01 update here , and Advanced Shader Delivery is also supported on AMD GPUs with Adrenalin 26.6.1 or higher and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X2 series with driver version 2026.08.3 or higher .

items.title: Mach9 raises $34M after pivoting to AI CAD software
items.summary: The startup initially set out to build better, faster, and cheaper surveying hardware in 2021.
items.content:
When Alex Baikovitz co-founded Mach9 Robotics in 2021, his goal was to build a better, faster, and cheaper way for civil engineers to do visual inspections. The company aimed to cut through red tape and modernize the slow, outdated processes that bog down construction in the United States.

Within a few years, Mach9 Robotics had built that hardware, but the effort led Baikovitz to a realization: hardware wasn’t the bottleneck.

“We saw how tedious it was for civil engineering organizations to take data from these amazing laser scanners and image data capture systems and turn that into a usable survey,” he told TechCrunch in an interview, referring to a detailed map of a site that engineers use for design work. “The real pain was in their workflows,” he said, and “how to turn all the endless amounts of data that they’re able to collect into . . .information that people can use to make the best design and asset management decisions across the board.”

So Baikovitz dropped “Robotics” from the company’s name and pivoted to developing AI-powered computer-aided design (CAD) software instead. The bet paid off, as Mach9 has racked up nearly 100 customers for the private beta of its software, and they’ve used it on more than 2,500 projects to date.

That momentum helped Mach9 unlock new funding. On Wednesday, the startup announced a $34 million Series A funding round co-led by First Round Capital and Bessemer Venture Partners. Also throwing in were Prudence, an early-stage, New York-based firm that focuses on investing in AI software use cases for construction and real estate, and Quiet Capital, a VC firm already on the cap table.

Mach9 is one of a number of startups racing to modernize the planning-to-building pipeline for construction and infrastructure. In August, a startup called CivilGrid raised $26 million to grow what it calls the “Google Maps for the underground.” Meanwhile, Blueprints AI , which uses AI to produce code-compliant, permit-ready architectural blueprints in just a few minutes, was among the top 200 companies in the Startup Battlefield competition at last week’s TechCrunch Disrupt.

Baikovitz said Mach9 is focused on disrupting CAD software because it’s one of the slowest and most labor-intensive pieces of that overall pipeline.

“It takes months to be able to deliver a project, and about a week per mile for someone to do manually in the legacy incumbent software that’s built by the Autodesk and Bentley Systems of the world,” he said.

Mach9 says its software automates a lot of that work, making the process 10 times faster and dramatically reducing costs. This allows customers doing surveying and civil engineering work to “expand their own capacity and take on more types of work, bigger projects, and expand the reach of how reality-capture data can influence major infrastructure decisions,” Baikovitz said.

Baikovitz said Mach9 developed and trained its own in-house AI models to reach the centimeter-accurate level that construction and infrastructure work requires.

“That’s not something that a lot of off-the-shelf models are able to do or deliver at in any capacity,” he said. “A big part of what our development process has looked like since 2024 has been, how do we build the industry leading models that can turn imagery or these multimodal image and laser scan data sets into survey grade like geometry, like tracing out the curbs, the pavement striping, all of this exactly how our customers want it to be at the accuracies that the industry demands.”

Mach9’s AI CAD system takes the survey data and creates a first draft of a plan, which engineers can then refine. The startup is “giving them all of the tools to draw, remove, adjust vertices, assess the quality of the AI-generated model, so that they can put effectively their name behind the deliverable that they’re producing, because there is a lot of liability in this particular industry, and it requires licensed professionals that know what they’re looking at,” Baikovitz said.

As for the funding, Baikovitz said his startup will split it between improving the product, hiring industry experts, and scaling “all parts of our organization to keep up with where the market is taking us.”

In retrospect, Baikovitz said he’s thankful that he initially went down the hardware path. It gave his startup something to pitch to potential customers, and it was largely those customers who told him they didn’t need better devices to capture data.

“I’m not interested in getting this cheaper, lower-cost hardware,” he remembers one VP telling him. But better software could “improve our efficiency in delivering these big statewide transportation mapping initiatives,” he said. He added that such projects help make states that Mach9 has worked with, like Texas, “much more like safe [and] effective.”

items.title: A Design Flaw in Share Links Exposes Users’ Personal Conversations With Meta’s Muse
items.summary: The company is suspending the feature after security researchers discovered how easy it was to access sensitive information shared with the AI assistant.
items.content:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.

Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people , the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.

Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:

“If you had asked us beforehand, we would have guessed that gathering these would take real effort,” the researchers wrote. “It took one query.”

In an emailed statement responding to questions from Ars, Meta said: “We opened the Muse bug bounty program so researchers could raise different scenarios and help us continue improving the product. People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link. However, we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.”

Asaf Aprozper, a cofounder and CTO of Claroc, said he reported the findings through Meta’s bug bounty program on October 8 and also tried reaching people at Meta on LinkedIn but got no reply either way.

The easiest way to discover the URLs is to perform a passive DNS search through one of many available commercial services. Passive DNS records store the historical resolution of domain names to IP addresses, as well as nameserver, and mail-server records over time. Passive DNS systems typically collect DNS responses from sensors positioned at recursive DNS resolvers or other infrastructure. A passive DNS record is generally created when a monitoring system observes a DNS response. In the case here, once the intended party clicks on the share link, the DNS information is recorded in a searchable database.

Claroc researchers were able to discover the Muse share links because all of them use the domain name cf.metaaiusercontent.com. Discovery is further made easy by the decision to add the conversation name to the URL, along with a long string of text. Simplified examples of such links are home-sale-budget-9f21c8a3.cf.metaaiusercontent.com, q3-revenue-review-7b1e42f0.cf.metaaiusercontent.com, and loan-application-draft-a4c9e2.cf.metaaiusercontent.com. It’s this last design decision, putting the conversation title in the subdomain rather than in the URL path, that makes public discovery possible.

“Plenty of AI assistants share by public link ,” Claroc said. “What makes Muse’s shares easy to find is the title sitting inside the web address, where public DNS records it for anyone to search. We call these GhostShares: pages that open for people who were never handed the link, and that those people can find on their own.”

Muse quickly catapulted to one of the top spots in Apple’s App Store. The assistant autonomously fills out forms, books appointments, makes purchases, creates documents, and carries out all kinds of other actions. To work as intended, Muse requires access to most of a user’s accounts. Meta has heavily marketed the assistant as a platform that’s worthy of the extraordinary trust it needs to work as intended.

Three weeks after the Muse launch, macOS security expert Patrick Wardle discovered a zero-day vulnerability that allowed any other app installed on the same device to gain complete control of the user’s Muse account. Meta downplayed the severity of the vulnerability on the grounds that exploitation wasn’t possible unless a device was already compromised. The company didn’t acknowledge Wardle’s finding that a simple ClickFix attack was all that was needed to hijack an account. The ease in discovering share links further justifies asking if Muse is worthy of the access it requires.

With Meta’s suspension of the feature, Muse users no longer face this particular threat, at least for now.

Spotify is busting free of CarPlay with the launch of its first native car app
items.summary: Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google's Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle's infotainment hardware - elimi
items.content:
Say goodbye to those aux cables. Spotify’s new in-car app is here, and it’s rolling out to Audi vehicles today.

Spotify announced Wednesday the launch of its next-generation, fully native in-car app, built directly on Google’s Android Automotive operating system. The standalone app, which is launching today in select Audi models, runs directly on the vehicle’s infotainment hardware — eliminating the need for phone tethering, Bluetooth connections, or aux cables.

Spotify’s new native app will launch with several Audi models, including the electric A6 e-tron and Q6 e-tron, as well as the gas-powered A5, Q5, and A6. Jonathan Tarlton, Spotify’s automotive business development lead, said the app, which has been in development for a little more than a year, is about delivering a more inviting experience to users — and specifically one that’s completely controlled by Spotify.

Spotify’s standard Android Automotive app operated as a “headless” integration, meaning that Spotify supplied the underlying backend data, playlists, and music catalog, but Google’s templates dictated how the interface was drawn and structured onscreen. The new Audi application is “headful,” allowing Spotify to draw and render its own native UI directly on the vehicle’s screens from scratch.

“We’re drawing all the pixels,” Tarlton said in an interview. “We own the user experience. So we’re not in a template or a framework. It’s 100 percent Spotify.”

To be sure, Spotify isn’t turning its back on Apple CarPlay and Android Auto; the company is still “heavily invested” in phone projection, Tarlton assured us. That said, the native Spotify app is being set up to compete directly with phone mirroring. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remain the default way many people listen to music or podcasts in their vehicles: Drivers get in, connect their phones automatically, and tap into their familiar mobile interface. A native Spotify app could encourage people to listen through the car’s own operating system instead of projecting their phones — a scenario that Tarlton says he welcomes.

“We’re drawing all the pixels. We own the user experience. So we’re not in a template or a framework. It’s 100 percent Spotify.”

“We want to give users choice,” he said. “We want to be wherever they are and we want to make sure that they’re accessing Spotify in the way they want to access it, whether they’re locked into the iOS ecosystem … or Android on the phone as well.”

People may love their CarPlay, but the experience is not without its tradeoffs. Wireless connection, in particular, can be spotty depending on your vehicle. Tarlton said the new app is aimed at reducing some of those headaches, like “a cold start in the morning,” he said. “You’re not having to wait to boot. You’re not having to wait for a screen to load. You’re not having to plug your phone in.”

There are other benefits to using the native Spotify app over a projected one from your phone. Passengers can scan a QR code displayed on the screen to join a wireless “Spotify Jam” session and add songs directly to the queue from their smartphones. On vehicles with a dedicated secondary passenger display, front passengers can browse, view lyrics, and watch video content without disturbing the driver. And while the vehicle is parked or charging, those motion graphics, like video podcasts and lyrics, move to the central display so everyone can enjoy.

With these features in particular, Spotify feels like it’s doing its part in helping to bring car passengers together again, Tarlton said. Often today you’ll find parents rocking out to their favorite hits in the front while kids are wearing their headphones in the back. The new app aims to correct that dynamic. “I’m excited that we can bring joy to the cabin again,” he said. “It’s not just technology.”

The rollout of the new Spotify app will focus in particular on cars with Android-based operating systems, he said. In that way, Spotifty can avoid having to build separate, bespoke applications for every individual automaker. Rather, the company can use a standard Android Automotive APK that it can then distribute through multiple app stores, whether it’s the Google Play Store or proprietary automaker stores like the Audi Application Store.

“Our number one goal was to prevent fragmentation, not just for our sake, but for the sake of the whole industry,” Tarlton said, “because we believe in having an open and fair place for apps to play — and the car is such a great place for that.”

items.title: I can’t get enough of the iPhone Duo’s matte inner display
items.summary: The iPhone Duo has all the messiness of a first-gen product. And while I'm not sure I love all of the decisions Apple made around its design, it got one thing right: the matte finish on the inner screen. I've been using it for the past week to watch movies on a plane, peruse my [
items.content:
Nano-texture was the right move.

Photography by Amelia Holowaty Krales

The iPhone Duo has all the messiness of a first-gen product . And while I’m not sure I love all of the decisions Apple made around its design, it got one thing right: the matte finish on the inner screen. I’ve been using it for the past week to watch movies on a plane, peruse my photo gallery, and catch up on a little reading, and I’m convinced. The matte screen is the best thing about the Duo, and I hope every other foldable maker copies it.

When we first got our hands on the Duo , the nano-texture finish on the 7.6-inch inner screen was genuinely a surprise. I’ve used a dozen or so book-style foldables over the past five years, and every one of them came with a glossy inner display. Aside from occasionally noting that they can be hard to see in direct sun, I never really questioned it. That’s just how screens are, I figured. But opening up the Duo for the first time, it clicked. Matte makes sense.

The benefits proved out while I used the phone for the past seven days. I propped it up on my tray table to watch an episode of Widow’s Bay . The matte screen effectively fought off the glare from the open window in my row. Reading a longer article felt a little easier on the eyes, and that’s what the inner screen is really there for. And there’s something about that slight matte finish that signals to my brain that it’s time to read . I can sort of fool myself into thinking that I’m holding an e-reader when I open the Kindle app and turn the phone sideways to its portrait orientation. It’s cute to imagine using your reading app in the landscape-oriented, partway-closed posture like a physical book. But I wouldn’t actually read anything like that; portrait all the way.

The thing to know about the Duo’s matte finish is that it’s pretty subtle. You don’t feel it under your finger quite as much as the more paperlike finish on TCL’s Nxtpaper devices. My colleague Dominic Preston wondered if it would be jarring flipping between the glossy cover screen and the matte display, and personally it hasn’t bothered me. The fact that the Duo’s big screen isn’t full-on e-reader matte probably helps ease that transition.

In fact, changing between the two screens somehow feels nice in both directions. Opening up to the inner screen feels like a welcome break from the reflections on the outer screen. When closing it and going back to the outer screen, the richer blacks and colors feel inviting.

I can concede that if you’re watching something with a lot of dark, shadowy scenes, the matte might feel like it obscures a bit of the detail that would otherwise stand out. It didn’t really bother me. But the bottom line is that this is a device that you will, by its nature, take outside. You’ll use it in ideal lighting conditions and crappy ones. I’ll take a slight hit in richness and detail for a more comfortable overall viewing experience. When my seatmate throws the window shade open, I’ll be ready for it.

items.summary: The iPhone Duo is the riskiest Apple product in years. It's a huge rethink of what an iPhone is and could be, and it contains the seeds of many fascinating ideas that might be great in the future. But that future is yet to come. The iPhone Duo is also one of Apple's messiest firs
items.content:
Apple’s first foldable is an early adopter special.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Photography by Amelia Holowaty Krales / The Verge

The iPhone Duo is the riskiest Apple product in years. It’s a huge rethink of what an iPhone is and could be, and it contains the seeds of many fascinating ideas that might be great in the future.

But that future is yet to come. The iPhone Duo is also one of Apple’s messiest first-generation products in a long time, and right now it will delight gadget nerds and early adopters and likely frustrate everyone else.

It’s been a minute since the iPhone has looked or worked significantly differently. The last major change was the iPhone X , which dropped the home button almost a decade ago, and even that was a fairly subtle improvement. In fact, “subtle improvement” is really the entire story of the iPhone — it’s the foundation of Apple’s entire business, after all, and there’s a lot of risk in just up and changing it. You can see it in this year’s iPhone 18 Pro : It’s been refined in many ways, with better thermals and an interesting variable aperture lens, but it’s barely different than the iPhone 17 Pro.

But you can’t play it safe designing a foldable. You have to make some big decisions about screen sizes and what the inner and outer displays are for, and then make an even bigger set of decisions about how that big inner screen should work. All of those decisions are risky, and Apple’s riskiest decision was the Duo’s size and shape.

Fun to play with Matte inner display is very cool You will watch less TikTok on it

You will watch less TikTok on it because the cover display is too small Heavier and bulkier than a standard phone Gets hot Cameras are just OK

Apple’s single most important design decision for the Duo was to make it shaped like a passport.

The wide aspect ratio makes the inner screen friendlier for 16:9 YouTube videos, but it also marks a departure from the taller foldable design phone makers have embraced over the past five years. Prior to 2026, most folding phones opted for a tall-and-narrow shape to optimize for using vertical apps on the cover screen. But rumors started pointing to Apple going with its landscape-first form factor, and other foldable makers shifted gears — seemingly to get ahead of Apple. Now that the iPhone and a handful of competitors have adopted the wide format, they have to solve a new problem: designing a cover screen that will work well enough for vertically oriented apps.

The Duo’s 5.4-inch outer display is glossy, while the 7.6-inch inner display has a striking nano-texture matte coating. Apple’s very proud of this inner matte display, and for good reason — it looks and feels incredibly solid, a big step up from foldables with glossy, seemingly soft screens with glaringly obvious creases, like the Pixel Fold, and even the more subtle but still visible crease of the Galaxy Fold 8.

The matte display is indeed there to help hide the crease, which Apple keeps calling “perceptually flat” because it’s more fun to invent science-y marketing phrases than just saying “you mostly don’t see it.” But it’s true: You mostly can’t see the display crease, although you can definitely feel it. If you’re looking at a white image off-axis, you can see it, and there are moments in some lighting where it’s much more obvious. It definitely shows up more prominently on camera than it does to your eyes.

What you will see is the under-display camera, which reflects light in a more glossy way if you’re outdoors or in a bright area. Overall, though, the camera and display crease stopped being noticeable after a while. The crease also wasn’t any more noticeable after a week of constant flipping and folding, although we’ll see how it holds up over time.

That’ll be a real test, because Duo owners are going to be constantly flipping this thing open. Between Apple’s display aspect ratio and iOS design choices, the outer screen feels like much more of a status display than you’d expect — everything about the Duo gently nudges you to flip it open and use it in tablet mode. And not just tablet mode, but portrait tablet mode. That’s because iPhone apps are largely portrait, and the Duo is still very much an iPhone, even though its shape makes it fight all that history.

iPhones have gotten bigger over the years, but they’ve mostly stuck to the same basic rectangular aspect ratios: 2:3 from the first iPhone through the 4S, 16:9 from the iPhone 5 through the 8, and 19.5:9 from the iPhone X on to today’s iPhone 18 Pro. Basically, the iPhone has mostly gotten taller over time.

It’s wild to have iPhone apps with controls in all kinds of different places

The Duo changes all of that — it’s the first iPhone that’s gotten shorter and wider. Both the inner and outer displays have a 1.4:1 aspect ratio, which was a very deliberate choice on Apple’s part, because they’re the same shape open and closed. This is clever in terms of display math and potentially great for app developers, but in practice it means that the outer display is really quite small, especially compared to modern Max-sized phones. If you’re texting someone in Messages with the keyboard onscreen, you’re lucky to be able to see two or three texts at once.

Apple has tried to reclaim some vertical space by scooting the UI elements of updated apps off to the right, but if you’re left-handed, that means using the phone closed with one hand can be challenging, even for someone with big hands. Having that strip of real estate along the right side occupied by navigation controls also means that using the Duo single-handed in your right forces you to reach farther when there’s something on the left side of the screen you need to tap. This means that you’re sometimes holding a fairly heavy phone, stretching for a small target that’s just out of reach, which isn’t particularly confidence-inspiring.

items.title: Apple iPhone Duo Review: Is It Worth It?
items.summary: Apple made an astonishingly good first foldable. Now iOS and third-party apps need time to catch up.
items.content:
It's a little hard to review the iPhone Duo. I've been toting Apple's first folding smartphone for the past week, and several apps I've tried to open on the sprawling 7.6-inch screen look awful. Thick, black bars on the sides, with a phone-sized app in the middle of this tablet-like display. But you likely won't encounter this problem once the Duo is in your hands.

In the past day, a handful of apps I use regularly updated to add full support for the iPhone Duo's screen sizes and vertical user interface elements. Instagram, Threads, Slack, and even the Google app now have navigational icons on the right rail instead of the bottom center, and the app content is better laid out to make use of the larger screen.

Developers need to target the iOS 27.1 software development kit (SDK) for full Duo compatibility. That will take some time. But it is a little maddening that some app developers, who for years have never seemed to care about optimizing their app for Android folding phones , are so quick to embrace Apple’s fold. Slack, for example, never offered the two-pane view of its desktop app in the Android version, but it's on the Duo. C’est la vie. Hopefully, Apple’s entry into foldables will result in a “rising tide lifts all boats” situation and Android fold lovers will get to enjoy those optimizations.

The iPhone Duo's Standby mode turns on when the phone is propped up via a kickstand.

The iPhone Duo arrives seven years after Samsung’s first Galaxy Fold . In Apple tradition, its first entry into an existing category feels fully mature; the Duo has significantly less jank than the first few generations of its Android counterparts . The infamous crease—where the phone folds—is hardly visible thanks to Apple’s display stack and clever use of a matte-finish nanotexture screen. The phone is IP68 dust- and water-resistant (though avoid taking the Duo to the beach, as sand is notoriously detrimental to phone hinges). The software experience, barring the unoptimized apps, feels carefully considered.

Apple has also landed on the right shape, months after Samsung realized it following seven years of narrow, somewhat awkward book-like folds . The wider, shorter “passport” design feels better than what’s come before in this category. The 5.4-inch outer screen is still big enough to be useful, and the hinge glides open gracefully and stays put at various angles. The hardware feels polished.

That’s not to say Apple has completely trounced the competition. I still appreciate that Samsung’s new Galaxy Z Fold8 is super lightweight at 201 grams, as the iPhone Duo’s hefty 254 grams (heavier than an iPhone 18 Pro Max ) can get tiring after extended doomscrolling. I don’t love the fact that, when closed, one side of the Duo has angled corners and the other is curved—the Fold8 looks better in that regard. Touch ID also takes a little getting used to after years of relying on Face ID, mostly when you’re holding the Duo with your left hand and you suddenly have to authenticate an app or purchase with your right hand. (It can mercifully auto-unlock if you're wearing an Apple Watch .)

Apple also tightly controls the multitasking experience. If you have two apps split-screen on the Duo, Apple won't let you resize one app to be slightly bigger than the other like you can on Android. Here, a 50-50 split is always enforced. You can't add a floating third app when in split-screen either, even though Apple has offered a similar capability on iPads for years. (The exception is video apps—you can have them float in picture-in-picture mode.) In portrait orientation, you can split-screen only with a video app; Apple won’t let you stack two apps, something Android has enabled for years.

That rigid software philosophy extends to basic input handling, too. I am typing this review on the iPhone Duo using a compact folding keyboard with a tiny attached trackpad. The trackpad works OK, but I could only get it to work after turning on AssistiveTouch in iOS’ accessibility settings. If the Duo is the iPhone that lets you do more, Apple should natively enable cursor support just like it does on iPads .

Then there are the physical quirks. The Duo supports MagSafe , so you can magnetically stick the phone to MagSafe tripods, mounts, and the like . (When it’s open, the Duo's weight makes the phone sag to one side.) But what about MagSafe wallets ? They’ll work, but Apple’s official wallet sticks out past the phone’s lower edge—not what you’d expect from a company that pores over every detail. Apple doesn’t have an official solution, so you’ll have to rely on a third-party accessory (and I suspect there will be many Duo accessories).

The iPhone maker follows the industry standard with a dual rear-camera system, lacking the third zoom camera from its Pro iPhones, which I sorely miss. At least the selfie cameras—the one on the outer screen and the “hidden” under-display inner camera seem to produce good results. On a Zoom call, my editor remarked that the video quality looked “really good” with both selfie shooters. (Zoom, by the way, wasn't optimized.)

When an app is properly optimized, the experience is chef’s kiss . Multi-pane views let you see a lot more in an app than candy-bar phones, a boost to productivity. Split-screening two optimized apps looks excellent, with plenty of room for each app to breathe and let you multitask. I haven’t found myself putting the Duo in angled positions much, mostly because I’ve really enjoyed using it with Apple’s Folio With Kickstand case, so much so that I wish the kickstand were integrated into the phone itself; I strongly recommend investing in an accessory to prop the Duo up.

Battery life has been pretty great. With average use, I’ve ended most days with around 40 percent left by bedtime. Right now, with over six hours of screen-on time because I’ve been working off the Duo for most of the workday, it’s almost 6 pm, and I’m at 45 percent. Impressive.

items.content:
A patch is about to roll out, but the exploit affects more than 40 percent of the internet.﻿

Security patches for the PHP programming language, widely used to build websites and web apps, are expected to roll out today, with the goal of fixing two critical vulnerabilities that could wreak havoc on the internet if left unchecked. In an advisory published on Tuesday , PHP developers said the vulnerabilities have a severity rating of 9.2 out of a possible 10, with some cybersecurity agencies encouraging websites to temporarily take their systems offline if they’re unable to apply the fix immediately.

The security patch is expected to drop today at 10AM ET — though the developers say they may release it earlier if the vulnerability details become public or there’s evidence of the exploits actively being used — and PHP users are being urged to “upgrade ​as soon as the release is available.” According to cybersecurity firm watchTowr , the vulnerabilities are Remote Code Execution exploits that reportedly impact every PHP version from PHP 5 onward, and could enable attackers to run their own code on affected servers, allowing them to maliciously alter websites, steal data, and more.

The impact of these vulnerabilities could be vast, with one security researcher estimating that more than 1.3 million internet-connected hosts are likely affected. WordPress security plugin provider Wordfence also warned that every WordPress site will be vulnerable because they all run on servers that use PHP, which is no small number given WordPress reported last year that it powers more than 40 percent of the internet . Wordfence also warned that the fix can’t be installed using automatic updates, so site owners need to find out who is responsible for updating PHP to apply the patch manually.

The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team and the UK National Cyber Security Centre have both issued advisories that encourage any companies who can’t immediately patch their platforms to instead isolate their internet-facing apps from public networks or take them offline entirely until the vulnerabilities can be fully mitigated. Mobile operating system developer GrapheneOS says they’ve temporarily taken their user discussion forum offline because proof of concept exploits are already being developed and they “don’t want to take the risk.” According to PHP developer Gina Peter Banyard, patching is the only mitigation, and otherwise turning servers off “might be the most sensible thing to do.”

Multiple cybersecurity organizations have also prompted PHP admins to prepare, with threat researchers at Sansec saying they expect to see “mass attacks within 15 minutes of the release.” That doesn’t mean attackers are waiting around, however. Cloudflare chief technology officer Dane Knecht says “we are seeing early attacks emerging” against the platform’s PHP sites, and that Cloudflare is temporarily updating its firewall rules as a stopgap until the fix is available.

함샤우트 글로벌이 AI 전문 자회사 딜라이트커뮤니케이션을 통해 오피스 솔루션 기업 퍼시스에 '생성형 AI 검색 최적화(GEO)' 통합 컨설팅을 제공했다.

21일 회사에 따르면, 이번 컨설팅은 B2B 구매·시설 실무자들의 핵심 정보 탐색 채널로 부상한 생성형 AI 환경에서 퍼시스의 공식 정보와 전문성 전달 체계를 정밀 진단하고 개선 전략을 수립하기 위해 추진됐다.

함샤우트 글로벌은 챗GPT·제미나이·퍼플렉시티 등 3개 모델에서 사무환경 관련 실무형 질문 80개를 바탕으로 총 480개 답변과 3332건의 인용 출처를 전수 분석했다. 아울러 공식 사이트의 AI 인용 준비도를 평가하는 디지털 자산 분석과 자체 개발 진단 솔루션 'AIBA'를 활용해 대표성·점유율·경쟁도·연관어·센티멘트 등 5대 지표를 업계 평균과 비교 측정했다.

분석 결과 퍼시스는 브랜드를 특정하지 않은 질문에서도 AI 답변 노출률 1위를 차지했으며, 퍼시스가 언급된 답변의 56.1%에서 복수 브랜드 중 가장 먼저 제시됐다. 자체 지표인 AIBA 브랜드 대표성 평가에서도 업계 평균 대비 약 1.7배 높은 점수로 1위를 기록했고, 공식 웹사이트 자산의 AI 출처 인용 건수 역시 최다를 나타냈다. 특히 3개 AI 모델 모두 퍼시스를 대기업 납품 실적과 전문성을 갖춘 '업무환경 솔루션 기업'으로 일관되게 규정했다.

함샤우트 글로벌은 이 같은 진단을 토대로 실무자 질문 대응 콘텐츠 기획, 공식 사이트 AI 인용 표준 템플릿, 분기별 지표 추적을 망라한 12개월 실행 로드맵을 수립했다.

공인희 함샤우트 글로벌 AI 연구소 소장은 “AI검색 환경에서의 브랜드 경쟁력은 얼마나 자주 노출되느냐가 아니라, 고객이 실제로 고민하는 질문에 얼마나 최신의 정확한 근거와 함께 언급되느냐로 결정된다”며 “이미 시장을 대표하는 브랜드가 AI 검색 채널까지 선제적으로 점검한 퍼시스 사례는 B2B 기업의 GEO 전략이 어디서 출발해야 하는지를 보여주는 기준이 될 것”이라고 말했다.

인터넷 입력 :2026/10/21 19:45

채널코퍼레이션이 음성 AI 상담을 지원하는 AI 전화 '보이스 알프'를 정식 출시하고, 고객에게 먼저 전화를 거는 '알프 마케팅'을 선보인다.

21일 회사에 따르면, 보이스 알프는 대화형 생성 AI 에이전트로 기존 채팅 상담 AI '알프'의 영역을 전화로 확장한 솔루션이다.

고객 문의에 응대하는 인바운드 상담은 물론, 특정 조건의 고객에게 AI가 자동으로 전화를 거는 아웃바운드 기능 '알프 마케팅'을 새롭게 지원한다. 이를 통해 잠재 고객의 B2B 영업 기초 상담이나 A/S 센터의 제품 정상 작동 확인 및 문자 안내 등을 자동화할 수 있다.

기술적 완성도 역시 끌어올렸다. 보이스 알프에는 고객의 억양과 머뭇거림을 분석해 발화 종료를 판단하는 '턴 감지(Turn Detection)' 모델이 적용돼 AI가 고객의 말을 끊는 현상을 최소화했다. 사내 카페의 AI 주문 데이터 1만여건을 분석한 결과, AI가 발화 미종료로 판단해 대기한 사례의 87%에서 1.5초 이내에 실제 요청이 이어진 것으로 확인됐다. 아울러 상담사 음성 데이터를 학습한 독자 한국어 음성 합성(TTS) 기술을 바탕으로 한·영 혼용 표현과 날짜, 시간, 웹 주소(URL)까지 자연스럽게 발음할 수 있도록 구현했다.

최완섭 채널코퍼레이션 최고제품책임자는 “아직도 전화 상담은 영업, 방문 예약, 결제 안내 등 기업 비즈니스 활동에서 보편적으로 사용되는 고객 상담 채널”이라며 “앞으로도 채널코퍼레이션이 지난 10여 년간 축적한 고객 상담 운영 역량과 AI 기술을 결합해 고객 전화 상담 경험을 혁신하는 데 주력하겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
"OLED 아이패드 3년째 판매 부진·메모리 값 급등 영향" 풀이

반도체ㆍ디스플레이 입력 :2026/10/21 19:35 수정: 2026/10/21 22:12

애플이 BOE 등 패널 업체에 액정표시장치(LCD) 아이맥 패널 개발 자료요청서(RFI:Request For Information)를 최근 보낸 것으로 21일 파악됐다. 애플 IT 제품 유기발광다이오드(OLED) 전환 속도조절론이 부상했다.

세트 업체는 RF I 단계에서 부품 업체에 개발 관련 기술 정보를 문의한다. 제품 사양을 결정한 뒤에는 견적의뢰서(RFQ:Request for Quotation)를 보낸다.

애플의 RFI 발송이 주목받는 이유는 해당 LCD 아이맥 출시 예상시점 때문이다. 최근 RFI를 보낸 제품은 2029년 전후 출시를 기대할 수 있다.

2029년은 애플이 첫 번째 유기발광다이오드(OLED) 아이맥을 출시할 수 있다고 업계에서 예상해온 '2029~2030년께'와 시기가 겹친다. 이미 삼성디스플레이는 대형 퀀텀닷(QD)-OLED 기술로 아이맥 OLED 프로젝트에 대응하고 있다. LG디스플레이는 대형 화이트(W)-OLED 기술로 아이맥 OLED 프로젝트를 진행하려 했지만 무산됐다.

애플이 BOE 등에 아이맥 LCD 개발 RFI를 보낸 사실이 알려지면서 업계에선 애플의 IT OLED 전환 신중론이 부상했다. OLED를 적용하면 제품이 얇아지고 명암비와 색 표현력 등에서 장점이 있지만 제조원가가 오른다.

애플이 지난 2024년 처음 출시한 OLED 아이패드 프로 판매가 3년째 부진한 데다, 올해 급등한 메모리 반도체 가격은 내년에도 상승할 것이란 전망이 우세하다. 존 터너스 애플 신임 최고경영자도 OLED 전환에 적극적인 편은 아닌 것으로 알려졌다.

업계 한 관계자는 "메모리 가격이 급등했기 때문에 애플은 OLED 아이맥의 가격 대비 성능을 고려해야 한다"며 "지금으로선 OLED 아이맥 출시를 서두를 이유가 없다"고 밝혔다. 다른 관계자는 " 애플이 (2029~2030년께) 첫 번째 OLED 아이맥과 LCD 아이맥 신제품을 함께 출시하는 '투 트랙' 전략도 예상할 수 있다"고 말했다.

애플이 BOE 등에 LCD 아이맥 패널 개발 RFI를 보내면서 LG디스플레이에는 LCD '스튜디오 디스플레이' 패널 개발 RFI를 보낸 것으로 알려졌다. 애플이 스튜디오 디스플레이에도 당장 OLED를 적용할 계획이 없다는 뜻으로 해석할 수 있다. 스튜디오 디스플레이는 본체가 별도로 없는 독립형 외장 모니터다. 맥북 등 애플 기기에 케이블을 꽂아 화면을 연결해 사용할 수 있다.

현재 아이맥 등 애플 하이엔드 IT 제품 LCD는 LG디스플레이가 주력으로 공급 중이다. 애플 LCD 공급망에는 LG디스플레이 외에 BOE, 티엔마 등이 있다. 티엔마는 화면이 작은 LCD 제품 위주로 대응 중이다. CSOT는 아직 애플 LCD 공급망에 없지만, 애플에 샘플을 보내며 LCD 공급망 진입을 노리고 있다.

한편, 삼성디스플레이 QD-OLED는 빛이 박막트랜지스터(TFT) 기판 반대 방향으로 나가는 전면발광 방식이고, 발광층이 5개인 5스택 제품(B-B-G-B-G)을 양산 중이어서 휘도(밝기)에서 강점이 있다. LG디스플레이 W-OLED는 빛이 TFT 방향으로 나가는 배면발광 방식인 데다, 아직 4스택 제품(B-G-B-R)까지 양산 중이어서 휘도에서 약점이 있다. 배면발광 방식에선 빛 일부가 TFT 기판에 가려진다.

LG디스플레이가 최근 온라인 기술 세미나를 개최한 플립(FLiPP) OLED는 향후 애플이 출시할 수 있는 OLED 스튜디오 디스플레이 납품을 노리는 것으로 알려졌다. 플립 OLED는 파인메탈마스크(FMM)를 사용하지 않고 노광으로 적녹청(RGB) OLED 서브픽셀을 패터닝하는 기술이다. 아직 양산성이 검증되진 않았지만 여러 패널 업체가 연구개발 중이다.

items.title: OpenAI Invests in Startup That Uses Brain Implants to Detect Cancer
items.summary: It’s the latest in a growing wave of bets that AI companies are making on brain data.
items.content:
OpenAI’s venture capital arm as well as Peter Thiel’s Founders Fund are investing in Coherence Neuro , a startup developing a brain implant to detect and treat cancer .

The investments are part of a $45 million seed funding round for Coherence and reflect Big Tech’s burgeoning interest in brain data . Coherence’s CEO and cofounder Ben Woodington says there is “growing synergy” between the big AI labs and companies building devices to decode the brain, known as brain-computer interfaces .

“The idea of capturing data to train better models and use it to optimize treatments is going to be super important,” he says. “The AI companies seem to be aligned with this thesis as well—that this novel data source is going to be valuable.”

Woodington says AI is a “perfect use case” for brain-computer interfaces because developers of these devices generate massive datasets that are too large for humans to analyze themselves. AI models can help read raw neural data and link it to actions, such as moving a computer cursor or producing synthesized speech.

In January, OpenAI announced that it was directly investing in a new brain-computer interface company, Merge Labs, cofounded by its billionaire CEO Sam Altman. Merge Labs came out of stealth with $252 million in initial funding to pursue ultrasound technology that can decode information from the brain. At the time, OpenAI said it was funding Merge Labs because of a belief that brain-computer interfaces “will create a natural, human-centered way for anyone to seamlessly interact with AI.” (The name Merge Labs comes from the idea popular in Silicon Valley that humans will eventually merge with machine intelligence.)

Thiel’s VC firm has also backed Elon Musk’s Neuralink as well as CTRL-labs, the creator of a wristband that translates neural signals from arm and hand movements that was acquired by Facebook in 2019.

Rather than focusing on restoring function for paralyzed individuals, San Francisco–based Coherence is developing AI models to decode subtle electrical signals associated with brain tumors. The company says it already knows how to detect these signals in animals to determine whether cancer is growing, shrinking, or recurring. The team is working to translate these findings for human research and, eventually, clinical trials.

This summer, Coherence briefly tested the recording ability of its implant in the brains of three people who were already undergoing brain tumor removal surgery at the Royal Melbourne Hospital in Australia. The implant was in place for roughly 30 minutes before being removed, providing an initial safety check. Next, Coherence is testing both the recording and stimulation capabilities of the device in an additional seven patients.

The implant is also designed to emit mild electrical stimulation to halt the growth of tumors. The idea is that over time, the device would learn to detect signals associated with cancer and provide real-time treatment. Coherence plans to use the new funding to launch a clinical trial to implant the device long-term in patients with glioblastoma, an aggressive type of brain cancer. The company also aims to develop implants to treat cancers in other parts of the body.

“Coherence's approach to developing a cancer therapy capable of improving from data is incredibly innovative,” Ian Hathaway, partner at the OpenAI Startup Fund, says in a statement. “We are proud to be backing them on this exciting mission.”

Woodington says that OpenAI will not have access to its data. “There's nothing in the contracts or arrangements that would mean that we would share, or they would have access to, any brain data or other health data that we're generating,” he says.

That is seemingly different from OpenAI’s relationship with Merge Labs. In its January announcement, OpenAI said it would “collaborate with Merge Labs on scientific foundation models and other frontier tools to accelerate progress.”

방미심위는 21일 서울 목동 방송회관에서 AI 채팅 서비스 사업자 15곳과 협력회의를 열고 유해 콘텐츠 차단과 청소년 보호조치 강화를 요청했다.

방미심위가 관련 서비스를 집중 점검한 결과 일부 AI 캐릭터의 이미지와 프로필, 상황 설명 등에 신체 부위를 과도하게 노출하거나 성적 행위를 암시하는 내용이 포함된 것으로 나타났다.

여성 캐릭터를 성적 대상화한 사례도 확인됐다.

이용자가 캐릭터를 선택해 대화하는 과정에서도 문제가 드러났다. 선정적인 질문이나 입력에 AI가 반응하면서 신체 노출과 성적 행위를 구체적으로 묘사하는 콘텐츠를 생성한 것이다.

방미심위는 “AI 채팅 서비스는 사업자가 선정한 AI 모델과 캐릭터·대화 상황의 설정 방식 등에 따라 그 결과와 유해성 정도가 달라진다”고 지적했다.

이에 따라 이용자가 입력하는 내용과 AI가 생성하는 답변을 모두 점검할 수 있도록 유해정보 탐지·차단 기능을 강화하고, 신고 체계도 개선할 것을 요구했다.

청소년 이용 가능 콘텐츠와 성인용 콘텐츠를 명확히 구분하고 성인용 콘텐츠에는 청소년유해표시를 적용하도록 했다. 본인인증을 거치더라도 우회 접속으로 연령 제한이 무력화되지 않는지 지속적으로 확인할 필요가 있다는 점도 강조했다.

회의에 참석한 사업자들은 청소년 보호 필요성에 공감하면서도 스타트업의 인력과 운영 여건에 따른 어려움을 전했다.

방미심위는 사업자 의견을 검토한 뒤 서비스별 유해성 수준과 청소년 접근 제한 조치의 실제 작동 여부를 조사해 오는 11월 심의를 시작할 계획이다.

The Best Hearing Aids I’ve Tested (2026): Jabra, Resound, Apple, and More
items.summary: These WIRED-tested devices will help you hear sounds more clearly. Never miss out on a dinner conversation again.
items.content:
Hearing-challenged individuals have long had one option for dealing with this widespread issue: an expensive, bulky hearing aid prescribed by a doctor. That changed in 2022 when the US Food and Drug Administration approved over-the-counter hearing aid devices, giving consumers access to a vast and growing array of alternatives. Today, there are more hearing aids than ever, and they come in different shapes, sizes, and most importantly, prices. How does a $100 hearing aid compare to a $4,000 prescription device for treating mild to moderate hearing loss? I’ve been testing products for the past four years to answer that question.

I’ve performed hands-on (ears-on?) testing of more than 65 hearing aid models around my home, outside, and in noisy environments. I’ve found plenty to like on the market today—and even more aids to avoid. The Jabra Enhance Select M3 holds the crown as the best over-the-counter hearing aid, while those seeking a prescription device should seek out a provider to fit them with a pair of Resound Sensia hearing aids. For those just getting started with hearing tech, I almost universally recommend giving Apple’s AirPods Pro 3 earbuds a try. They’re an intuitive way to see how your hearing can improve without breaking the bank.

Below is my complete roundup of the best prescription and over-the-counter hearing aids I’ve tested and approved.

Updated October 2026: I've updated my picks with the Jabra Enhance Select M3, Resound Sensia 9, Oticon Zeal, and Legato Harmony Glasses.

What to Consider Before You Buy

Every person is unique, and so are their hearing loss needs. Consider these factors to find a device that suits your needs and lifestyle. For more tips, check out our How to Buy a Hearing Aid guide.

Hearing aids shouldn’t bankrupt you. With such a steep price and minimal insurance coverage, it’s no wonder that so many people put off hearing loss treatment. Between audiologist visits, hearing aid orders, custom fittings, and maintenance, it’s justifiable that you might postpone treatment rather than fork over your credit card. It’s vital you know your budget before you start browsing for hearing aids. Many brands offer trial periods where you can test out the devices for a set number of days and, if they're a bad fit, return them free of charge.

It doesn’t have to be obvious that you’re wearing a hearing aid. Despite cartoonish media depictions of hunched-over seniors screaming “WHAT?!” at every person who tries to talk to them, hearing loss doesn’t discriminate by age. With nearly 10 million Americans under the age of 60 affected, more should be taking advantage of the sleekly designed hearing aids on the market. Similar to the stigmas that keep people from seeking mental health treatment , the hearing-loss community is plagued by self-consciousness when it comes to wearing these devices. Modern in-the-ear (ITE) hearing aids have come a long way in subtlety.

Opt for a professional hearing test over an online one. While online and app-based tests are a good way to dip your toes in and see whether you have hearing loss, a detailed audiogram that only an in-office visit can provide is a far better option. A hearing professional can use this audiogram to calibrate hearing aids to your specific needs.

What Are the Different Types of Hearing Aids?

Before you choose which hearing aid is right for you , it’s best to familiarize yourself with the different styles on the market. While you may see multiple design styles, hearing aids essentially boil down to two main varieties: behind-the-ear and in-the-ear. Completely in-canal (CIC) devices also exist, but none are available over the counter. Here are common terms you’ll see:

Behind-the-ear (BTE) hearing aids , also known as over-the-ear, are probably the most traditional style. For these devices, an often bulky plastic case rests on the back of your ear while a tube delivers sound to an ear mold. Because they’re bigger, they tend to have the most technology and can cater to higher degrees of hearing loss. That said, they also tend to stand out more, which is a drawback for those looking for subtlety. Receiver-in-the-ear (RITE) hearing aids are essentially the same as behind-the-ear devices, with a receiver component that sits in the ear canal instead of being built into the case. Though the industry likes to tout them as a sleeker, less noticeable counterpart, in actuality, they’re not much smaller than BTEs and function identically.

In-the-ear (ITE) hearing aids, also known as in-the-canal (ITC), are more comparable to wireless earbuds from a design standpoint. These devices allow for directional mics but also tend to collect moisture and wax.

Completely in-canal (CIC) hearing aids are the most “invisible” hearing aids on the market. This is because, as the name suggests, they’re completely submerged in your ear canal with nothing sticking out (besides a tiny string for removal). They typically have to be inserted by a professional and left in the ear for longer periods, and as noted, they are not available over the counter.

Self-Fitted vs. Preset Hearing Aids

Traditional hearing aids must be “fitted”—not just physically fitted to your ear anatomy but acoustically fitted to line up with the particulars of your hearing loss. This is because for most people, hearing loss is not unilateral. Some may experience trouble hearing low frequencies, while others may struggle with higher ones. (Mine has a dip somewhere in the middle.) By tuning the hearing aid to boost the frequency bands where your hearing is at its weakest, a precision hearing aid can improve your overall hearing quality without blowing out the frequencies where your ears are already working well.

인공지능(AI) 기술이 발전하면서 사이버 공격이 빠르고 정교해졌다. 랜섬웨어, 비즈니스 이메일 침해, 공급망 공격 등 중소기업을 노린 위협도 늘고 있다. 대기업과 공공기관이 협력업체에 요구하는 보안 수준도 높아지는 추세다.

SK쉴더스 분석 결과 중소·중견기업이 침해를 인지하고 조사에 착수하기까지는 평균 106일이 걸렸다. 과학기술정보통신부와 한국인터넷진흥원(KISA)에 따르면 올해 상반기 랜섬웨어 신고는 145건으로 76.8% 늘었다.

이번 MOU는 중소기업의 보안 역량 강화로 사전 예방을 돕고, 혹시 모를 사이버 침해 사고 시에는 보험을 통해 기업의 리스크를 줄이겠다는 전략으로 풀이된다.

SK쉴더스는 이노비즈협회 약 7800개 회원사에 무료 보안 컨설팅과 관리형 탐지 및 대응(MDR) 서비스를 제공한다. MDR은 위협 탐지부터 분석, 대응까지 보안 전문가가 직접 수행하는 서비스다.

24시간 위협 모니터링과 침해사고 대응을 지원하고, 사이버보안 세미나로 최신 위협 동향도 공유한다. SK쉴더스는 AI 기반 관제 플랫폼 '시큐디움'과 침해사고 대응 조직 '탑서트'를 기반으로 서비스를 운영한다.

DB손해보험은 중소기업 환경에 맞춘 사이버보험으로 사고 이후 재정 부담을 덜고 사업 정상화를 돕는다. 이노비즈협회는 회원사가 보안 서비스와 사이버보험을 쉽게 활용하도록 안내하고, 보안 인식 제고 프로그램을 공동 추진한다.

현지 시청자 공략 '로컬 퍼스트' 전략과 실무 제작 노하우 공유

방송/통신 입력 :2026/10/21 18:46

넷플릭스는 영화진흥위원회와 협력해 영화 영상 산업 종사자와 예비 영화인 100여 명을 대상으로 글로벌 역량 강화 교육을 진행한다고 21일 밝혔다.

교육은 11월10일 한국영상자료원 시네마테크에서 열린다. 2023년부터 이어온 K콘텐츠 인재 양성 업무협약의 일환이다.

교육은 두 가지 주제로 진행된다. 첫 번째는 현지 시청자 정서와 문화에서 출발하는 ‘로컬 퍼스트’ 기획 전략이다. 한국 콘텐츠 고유한 매력을 세계에 전하는 방향을 다룬다.

두 번째는 넷플릭스 프로덕션의 이해를 통해 창작자의 비전을 구현하는 제작 과정과 파트너사 협업 방식을 설명한다.

넷플릭스는 그간 영진위와 KAFA 마스터클래스, 멘토링 등 신진 영화인을 위한 교육과 교류를 지원해왔다.

여러 영화제 후원과 단편영화 상영을 통해 신진 창작자가 글로벌 관객을 만날 기회를 지속해서 넓혀가고 있다.

넷플릭스 관계자는 “영진위와 넷플릭스 기획, 제작 경험을 나누고 차세대 영화인이 자신만의 이야기를 작품으로 완성할 수 있는 기회를 꾸준히 마련하겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
22일 ‘2026 과학기술사업화·ASTI 리더스 포럼'서 공개

과학 입력 :2026/10/21 18:44 수정: 2026/10/21 18:45

인공지능(AI) 기반 과학기술사업화 플랫폼 '아폴로(APOLLO) 2.0’을 공개하는 자리가 마련됐다.

한국과학기술정보연구원(KISTI)은 22일 JW 메리어트 동대문 스퀘어 서울에서 개최하는 ‘2026 과학기술사업화·ASTI 리더스 포럼’에서 이를 공식 런칭할 예정이다.

이 플랫폼은 국가 R&D 성과를 실제 산업 현장과 연결하기 위해 구축된 국내 최초의 AI 기반 기술사업화 분석 플랫폼이다.

기업 특성을 분석해 사업화 유망성이 높은 국가 R&D 성과를 알려주거나, 국가 R&D 성과를 검색하면 이를 활용할 수 있는 수요기업과 적용가능한 제품·시장을 찾아준다.

KISTI는 이 아폴로 버전을 ASTI와 연계, 지역 산업 현장의 AI 전환(AX)을 추진 중이다. 아폴로가 데이터와 AI 기술을 통해 '기술-기업 매칭 솔루션'을 제공하면 ASTI는 플랫폼을 활용할 현장을 실시간 잇는 '휴먼웨어(Humanware)' 역할을 한다. ASTI는 전국 9,000여 개 기업 및 14,000여 회원으로 구성된 민간 협의체다.

KISTI는 이날 기술이전에서부터 신사업 아이템 발굴 등 공공 R&D 성과가 지역 산업 현장으로 빠르게 스며드는 구체적인 연결 로드맵을 보여줄 계획이다.

KISTI는 자체 개발한 AI 기반 과학기술사업화 플랫폼 ‘아폴로(APOLLO) 2.0’과 KISTI가 운영중인 과학기술정보협의회(ASTI)의 기업·지역 네트워크를 연계, 국가 R&D 성과가 기업 혁신 및 지역산업 성장으로 이어지는 체계 구축을 추진할 방침이다.

한편 이번 포럼 주제는 ‘AI 대전환과 과학기술사업화, 국가 R&D 성과를 기업과 지역의 성장동력으로’로 마련됐다. 이식 KISTI 원장 개회사를 시작으로 최문기 과학기술정보통신부 연구성과혁신관, 송혜자 국가인공지능전략위원회 지역특별위원회장, 김병국 과학기술사업화진흥원장 등이 축사, 김병국 과학기술정보협의회장 환영사 등이 환영사를 준비했다.

기조연설은 정희권 연구개발특구진흥재단 이사장이 맡았다. 이어 정지성 에스오에스랩 대표가 ‘딥테크 기업이 필요로 하는 공공기술과 사업화 지원’을, 김영록 넥스트챌린지 대표가 ‘탈패턴 인재: 딥테크의 격차’를 주제로 강연한다.

이식 원장은 "새롭게 런칭하는 아폴로 2.0과 ASTI의 탄탄한 기업 지원 역량을 결합해 국가 R&D 성과 확산의 새로운 지평을 여는 자리가 될 것”이라며 “AI와 지역 AX 전환을 통해 대한민국 과학기술사업화 생태계가 한 단계 도약하는 계기가 될 것"으로 기대했다.

items.content:
경찰, 450억 예산 투입…지방청 18곳·경찰서 262곳에 1대 이상씩

IT 일반 입력 :2026/10/21 18:39 수정: 2026/10/21 18:40

김종철 경찰청장 직무대행이 21일 "경찰 관서마다 순찰로봇을 한 대 이상 보급할 계획"이라고 밝혔다.

김 대행은 이날 인천 송도컨벤시아에서 열린 제8회 국제치안산업대전에서 치안 분야에 로봇·인공지능(AI)을 활용하는 방안을 설명하면서 이 같이 말했다.

현재 전국 경찰서는 262곳, 시도경찰청은 18곳이다. 모두 280곳에 로봇을 들이는 구상이다. 경찰청은 이를 위해 내년 예산안에 범죄예방 로봇 450억원을 새로 편성했다. 내년에 순찰로봇 300대 도입을 추진하며, 로봇 규격과 운영체계를 마련할 연구용역도 진행 중이다.

대테러 대응 로봇 48억원, 경찰부대 보조 로봇 40억원 등을 더한 인공지능 로봇 예산은 560억 5000만원이다. 고위험 피해자 주거지에 설치하는 지능형 폐쇄회로TV(CCTV) 예산 22억 8000만원도 담겼다.

김 대행은 로봇이 당장 맡을 수 있는 역할에는 한계가 있다고 선을 그었다. 그는 "(로봇은) 순찰을 도는 지역경찰관을 보조하는 역할"이라면서 "시민이 눈으로 느끼는 체감도를 높이는 정도로 기대하고 있다"고 말했다.

로봇 순찰이 반복돼 데이터가 쌓이면 정부 차원의 육성과 집중 투자로 이어질 수 있다고 설명했다. 보급 과정에서 기술적 한계 등을 종합해 소외되는 지역이 없도록 하겠다는 취지로 답했다. 농어촌 지역 등을 염두에 둔 발언으로 풀이된다.

경찰은 이미 현장에서 시범 운영을 하고 있다. 수원팔달경찰서는 지난해 11월부터 수원특례시, 로봇 기업 도구공간과 함께 수원 화성행궁 일대에서 순찰로봇 '팔달봇'을 운영 중이다. 밤 10시부터 새벽 4시까지 하루 네 차례 순찰하며, 비명이나 낙상 같은 이상 행동을 감지하면 관제센터와 인근 파출소에 알린다.

서울 서남권에서는 지난 6월부터 인공지능(AI) 순찰차 1호차를 운행하고 있으며, 하반기에 2호차와 3호차를 추가한다. 내년에는 비명 같은 위급 음성을 인식하는 소리 인공지능을 넣는다. 2028년 이후에는 112상황실과 원격으로 연결하는 체계를 추진한다.

경찰청은 지난 3월 미래치안정책과를 치안인공지능정책과로 바꿔 경찰 내 AI 사업을 총괄하게 했다. 민원 응대를 돕는 '모두의 경찰관'은 내년 12월까지 개발한다. 올해는 경찰관 업무 지원 기능을, 내년에는 시민이 직접 쓰는 챗봇을 내놓는 일정이다.

이재명 대통령은 이날 경찰의 날 기념식에서 범죄를 사후에 수습하는 데서 사전에 예방하는 쪽으로 치안의 무게를 옮기라고 주문했다. AI 기반 차세대 112시스템 구축에도 속도를 내 달라고 당부했다.

경찰청은 이날 싱가포르 내무부 산하 홈팀과학기술청(HTX)과 업무협약을 맺고 인공지능과 로봇 치안기술 공동 연구에 나서기로 했다.

로봇, AI를 치안에 활용하는 데 대해 김 대행은 "시작은 미미할 수 있지만 나중에 정말 기대해도 될 것 같다"고 말했다.

정부가 추진하는 차세대발사체 재사용 기술 개발의 후속 사업을 선제적·구체적으로 준비해야 한다는 지적이 제기됐다.

한준호 의원(국회 과학기술정보방송통신위원회 소속)이 21일 우주항공청으로부터 제출받은 자료에 따르면, 우주청은 액체산소와 메탄을 추진제로 하는 재사용 가능 차세대 발사체를 개발 중이다. 올해부터 오는 2032년까지 2조 2,921억원이 투입된다.

목표는 수직이착륙을 위한 '호핑시험' 등 재사용 핵심기술 검증이다. 엔진 추력조절과 정밀 유도제어, 착륙 정밀도 등 재사용 핵심기술을 기술성숙도(TRL) 6 수준까지 확보할 계획이다.

모자란 부분에 대한 후속 기술 개발 계획도 있다. 오는 2033년부터 2035년까지 재진입 제어와 1단 회수, 정비·재발사 기술 등을 확보하고 기술성숙도 TRL 8 수준에 도달하는 방안을 검토중이다.

우주청은 예산 수요로 912억원을 제시했다. 1단 발사체 회수·유지보수 관련 기술개발에 412억 원, 해상착륙 플랫폼인 드론쉽 개발에 500억 원이 필요할 것으로 예상했다.

이에 대해 한준호 의원은 "2032년까지 핵심기술을 검증한 뒤 실제 발사체 회수와 재발사 기술을 확보하기 위해서는 2033~2025년의 후속 기술 개발이 안정적으로 이어져야 한다”며 “2032년 이전에 후속사업 기획 및 예산확보 절차를 선제적으로 준비해야 기술개발 연속성을 확보할 수 있을 것"이라고 지적했다.

한 의원은 "우주청은 오는 2035년 재사용 기술 확보 목표를 안정적으로 달성할 수 있도록 체계적인 이행계획을 구체적으로 수립해 달라"고 주문했다.

Eight Bits of Trust; eMudhra's CA keys cracked in milliseconds
items.summary: Article URL: https://scotthelme.co.uk/eight-bits-of-trust-emudhras-ca-keys-cracked-in-milliseconds/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50177916 Points: 366 # Comments: 145
items.content:
One of eMudhra's certificate authority private keys is the number 4.

Not a number that starts with 4, or the number 4 followed by a few hundred random digits, just, 4... Another one is 56, and another is 115. I know, because I recovered all of them from their public certificates on my laptop just now, and it took less than a second.

On Saturday 17th October a security researcher reported to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Mozilla and eMudhra that the private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificates were compromised. Chrome pushed a CRLSet update blocking them that evening and Mozilla blocked them in Firefox via OneCRL a few hours later. On Tuesday 20th, Mozilla announced it publicly and shipped an NSS update removing the eMudhra root, and Chrome confirmed the root is going in Chrome Root Store v43.

The eight intermediates are six TLS issuing CAs (DV, OV and EV, two generations each) and two code-signing CAs, all created in April 2025. Every one of them was also cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root in May 2025.

That's the "what", but it's the "how" that's the interesting part, and it was summed up in one line on the thread by Ian Carroll:

These are elliptic-curve keys on the P-384 curve. The private key is just a number, d . The public key, the thing that goes in the certificate for the world to see, is d × G , where G is a fixed point on the curve that everyone uses and "×" means adding G to itself d times using the curve's special arithmetic.

Going forwards is easy, but going backwards, from the public key to d , is considered to be impractical. That's the entire security model, and it only holds if d is enormous. A P-384 private key should be a random 384-bit number, which gives you 2³⁸⁴ possibilities (or roughly 10¹¹⁵), so nobody is ever going to search that.

eMudhra's keys look like this:

A P-384 private key should look like this:

That's 47 bytes of zeros and then one byte, and all eight keys are like that. A single byte has 256 possible values, so the "search" is: compute 1 × G , 2 × G , 3 × G , and stop when it matches the certificate, which is at most 255 steps.

So the whole thing, every certificate those CAs could ever issue, every client that trusted them, rested on eight bits.

Mozilla attached the affected certificates to their announcement, so I pulled all 16 (8 keys, each used in two issued certificates: once by eMudhra and once by Sectigo) and brute-forced them. Every single one fell over instantly, the six TLS values, and the two code-signing keys are just as weak:

It's interesting that nothing about these certificates looks wrong. A public key derived from d = 4 is a perfectly valid point on the curve, the encoding is fine, the curve is fine, every structural check passes. The only way to find out is to try.

Normally when a CA key is compromised, someone stole it! There's a thief, there's a moment it happened, and you can at least reason about who now has access to that key.

Here, nobody had to steal anything. The key was effectively public from the day the certificate existed. Anyone who looked at one of these certificates, at any point since April 2025, could have recovered the key in milliseconds on commodity hardware. That's a 17 month window and there is no way to know whether someone did.

Chrome made the point that because Chrome enforces Certificate Transparency, and no TLS certificates chaining to these CAs ever showed up in CT, no forged certificate could have been trusted by default in Chrome. That's true and it's reassuring for browsers. CT detects mis-issuance though, it doesn't prevent it, and a lot of software doesn't check CT at all.

Mainstream and updated browsers are likely absolutely fine. Chrome and Firefox block the intermediates directly and both require CT, and Safari requires CT too.

Everything else is a different story, though. Most non-browser TLS clients (so basically everything else, with default settings), things like curl, Python, Node, Go, Java, git, package managers and every script and daemon you've got, do three things that matter here: they trust a CA bundle on disk, they don't check revocation by default, and they don't check CT. So the fact that eMudhra and Sectigo have revoked these intermediates doesn't help them at all. This is something that I find often when talking about TLS and PKI, understanding just how massive the client ecosystem is can be overlooked. We often focus on this in training when we look at modern solutions for revocation like CRLite, which works wonders on the desktop browsers, but does nothing for any other TLS client. Consider what needs its root store updating now, and this is just the tip of the iceberg:

I tested this on my own machines using a local server and a certificate for api.stripe.com , a name that we can all likely agree is very high value. With default settings, curl said SSL certificate verify ok , Python completed the handshake, and Node said authorized: true . That was true on every Linux and macOS machine I tested. On Windows, CryptoAPI accepted the chain unless revocation checking was switched on, and even then only one of the two routes came back as revoked.

You can put any other hostname you want in that certificate and you have everything you need to intercept that device's traffic, all you have to do is get on the network path.

It's fortunate that the steps required here aren't particularly complicated for the devices you can update, and the advice essentially boils down to 'update them'. The problem is the devices you can't update or update easily.

Eight bits. For 17 whole months, that's all that stood between a huge amount of non-browser software and a forged certificate for any site blowing the security on all of your encrypted traffic.

items.title: The 1.5°C goal of the Paris Agreement is no longer viable
items.summary: Article URL: https://unric.org/en/unep-emissions-gap-report-2026-1-5-degree-overshoot/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50177911 Points: 480 # Comments: 544
items.content:
The target set in 2015 by the Paris Agreement—to limit global warming to 1.5°C by 2100—has become unachievable within the span of a single decade, the United Nations Environment Programme ( UNEP ) notes in its 2026 Emissions Gap Report.

“The opportunity to bridge the 1.5°C emissions gap with ‘no or limited’ overshoot has been lost,” states the report, titled “ The Point of Return .”

Exceeding the 1.5°C threshold above pre-industrial levels is now imminent and inevitable.

“Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C raises the risk of irreversible changes including in ice sheets, permafrost carbon, ocean circulation and coral systems, along with devastating human impacts,” the report states.

The urgent task is to ensure that global warming remains below the 2°C threshold, with the aim of returning to 1.5°C by the end of the century. This is the only option left, according to UNEP.

To achieve this, global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions would need to be reduced by 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, and 69% by 2040, relative to 2025 levels.

The current trajectory falls far short of this. Even assuming that the commitments made by governments—known as nationally determined contributions (NDCs)—are fully implemented, emissions would only be reduced by 5% to 8% by 2030 and by 11% to 15% by 2035, compared to 2025 levels.

The recommended efforts are “close to 6 per cent every single year until 2035,” declares the UN Secretary General.

The UN Chief outlined the levers for action available to humanity:

“The emissions gap is now a leadership gap. And the world is running out of time and excuses to close it.

Governments must go much further and faster. Accelerate clean energy and electrification across every sector.

Adopt credible roadmaps to transition away from fossil fuels – with clear timelines and protection for affected workers and communities.

Invest in grids and storage. Improve energy efficiency. Cut methane emissions. Halt and reverse deforestation.”

The report indicates that by 2035, the capacity of renewable energy sources must triple compared to 2025 levels. Furthermore, the phase-out of fossil fuels requires reducing the respective shares of coal, oil, and gas in energy production by 55%, 15%, and 5% by 2035.

By 2040, reductions of at least 75%, 30%, and 35% would be necessary.

Large-scale operations to remove CO2 from the atmosphere will also be imperative to return to the 1.5°C threshold—or even lower.

UNEP estimates that 320 gigatons of CO2 —equivalent to eight times the emissions recorded in 2024— must be removed from the atmosphere by the end of the century. This implies biological solutions, such as reforestation, as well as technological approaches involving the compression, mineralisation, and underground storage of CO2.

Accelerating the momentum is still possible, according to UNEP, given the significant progress made since 2015.

“Since the adoption of the Paris Agreement, global renewable electricity capacity has grown three times faster than anticipated, with solar PV build-out increasing seven times faster”, states UNEP Chief Inger Andersen.

“Total energy supply from coal and oil has grown slower than projected. Climate policies have delivered real emission reductions across the world and across sectors. Several G20 members have shown sustained emission reductions, and some are aligning policies with net-zero pledges.”

The progress made remains insufficient, particularly with regard to fossil fuels and deforestation.

Because the climate knows no borders, limiting any overshoot of 1.5°C as much as possible requires action across the entire economy and on a global scale.

items.content:
I’d wager everyone has a rehearsed response to what’s absolutely one of the world’s worst interview questions: “What’s your biggest weakness?” Whenever I’ve gotten it, I take a slow—even pensive—breath and rattle off my line: “I say no to myself too much.”

I won’t lie. It’s a bit shameless—a definite humblebrag. I’m a systems thinker: When an idea pops up, I immediately spin up a feasibility assessment in my head. I run lists, plot timelines, and tally budget line items. Sometimes a rough Gantt chart starts to take shape. (I’m a gas at parties, as you can surely tell.)

My brain, throughout my 20-plus-year career as a science and tech journalist, has played host to a near ­constant tug-of-war between ambition and reality. Learning to find that balance is a big part of what’s helped me survive in this industry and, ultimately, led me here. This past spring, I had the great privilege of joining the incredible team of journalists behind MIT Technology Review to take the reins of the print magazine.

If you’ve been reading along with us for the last handful of issues, you may have noticed a few changes starting to materialize. We’ve brought back a regular roster of lists and infographics (both things that magazines do particularly well). But the biggest change is only just beginning to take shape, which is why Mat Honan, our editor in chief, asked me to hop in to introduce myself—and the issue you’re holding in your hands right now.

We’re giving ourselves permission to play around and experiment. To be a little … audacious.

Because, practical though I may be, I do still have plenty of ideas. It’s just that I sometimes need a reminder to stop blocking myself and do the thing . That’s the spirit driving this issue in particular.

We wanted to end 2026 with a slate of stories that check in on impossible ideas. Why? Because it’s frankly a lot of fun to dream about living on the moon or uploading our brains. Because losing sight of ambition is all too easy when it feels as if we’re playing whack-a-mole with the world’s problems. But also because the scientists and engineers who absolutely refuse to give up on even the most daring endeavors—like making synthetic blood or decoding animals’ speech—remind us what this whole technology thing is supposed to do to begin with.

It’s supposed to take cutting-edge research and development and apply it to make life better, safer, healthier, even more joyful. And when we eff up and make things worse (see: forever chemicals, traffic deaths, and AI that encourages potentially dangerous user behavior), we’re supposed to dig back in, assess the damage, and find ways to fix what we’ve broken. Even when unraveling the mess might itself seem impossible.

So yeah, this one’s for the folks who have the audacity to try, and who refuse to let anyone—themselves included—tell them no.

I hope you enjoy the ride.

items.content:
Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era of more efficient, potentially faster spaceflight—saving astronauts time and cutting their exposure to harmful cosmic radiation as they travel to Mars and beyond. “You wake up to that announcement, and it puts a big smile on your face,” says Simon Middleburgh, co-director of the Nuclear Futures Institute at Bangor University in Wales.

Running a nuclear reactor in space may sound like lunacy, but it’s not. The Soviet Union sent dozens of reactors into orbit, often to power spy satellites. And experts say there aren’t any major technical obstacles to making nuclear space propulsion happen. “I think it’s a very doable technology,” says Philip Metzger, a spaceflight engineering researcher at the Florida Space Institute.“I’m happy to see them finally doing this.”

Still, developing space propulsion using reactors has been slow going. The US has started—and terminated— several programs looking into it over the past 75 years. The latest casualty was DRACO, a collaboration between NASA and the Department of Defense, which ended in 2025. The project was canceled because of high experimentation costs, an inability to compete with conventional rocket propulsion on price, and difficulty ensuring that ground tests could be performed safely and effectively. (You are creating an incredibly powerful nuclear reaction, after all.)

After much wavering, it now appears that nuclear-powered interplanetary travel is a $2 billion bet NASA is willing to make. The agency is pursuing an approach called nuclear electric propulsion, which uses the neutrons produced in a self-­sustaining, uranium-­atom-splitting reaction to create heat and ultimately electricity. The electricity is used to ionize a gas, which is blasted out of the spacecraft with the help of magnetic fields, generating thrust. The approach “is very low thrust, but very efficient,” says Sebastian Corbisiero, the US Department of Energy’s national technical director of space reactor programs. “So you can use it for a long period of time.”

What might such a rocket look like? A presentation by Steve Sinacore, program director of NASA’s SR-1 program, offers some clues. So far, the concept art makes the craft look like a colossal fletched arrow. The back will house the power-and-propulsion system, while the tip will hold a uranium-filled nuclear reactor with a capacity of at least 20 kilowatts. (For context, a typical nuclear plant on Earth is about 50,000 times more powerful.) The “fletches” on SR-1 are large fins that help cool the reactor by radiating heat into space.

Like many other pieces of space hardware, the reactor will need to be put through its paces on the ground before it’s cleared for the rough rocket trip to space. “Going through the launch safely is going to be a challenge,” says Middleburgh. “You are being shaken, rattled, and rolled.” For safety reasons, the reactor will be switched on around two days post-launch, when it’s comfortably far from Earth. Uranium isn’t tremendously dangerous by itself, but that can’t be said of the waste products that emerge when the reactor is running. If SR-1 works as planned, its journey to Mars will take about a year.

Will this novel form of space propulsion actually reach the Red Planet by 2029? It’s possible. NASA says the Idaho National Laboratory, which is building SR-1’s reactor, is making progress and is on target for a late-2028 launch. “Procurement of major components is underway, and integration work on the power and propulsion element is advancing steadily,” Sinacore told MIT Technology Review . The outlook will get even sunnier if the Artemis program, which aims to start laying the foundations for a base on the lunar south pole by the decade’s end, keeps to its own bold deadline.

“It’s an aggressive timeline,” says Lindsey Holmes, who is vice president of advanced projects at Analytical Mechanics Associates, an aerospace company in Virginia. She suspects the push is being driven partly by China’s and Russia’s own deep-space nuclear ambitions . The two countries have spoken about plans to place a reactor on the moon’s surface in the mid-2030s to power a jointly operated lunar base. Whether it flies or fails in space, SR-1’s development should help NASA put its own reactor on the moon; the technology involved in the two projects is broadly similar, given that the lunar surface, like space itself, is a vacuum. If an interplanetary nuclear-powered spacecraft works, a nuclear reactor on the moon should too.

Most of the technology for SR-1 already exists; it’s going to come down to piecing it all together and then seeing how it performs in space.

items.title: Solid-state batteries
items.summary: The rise of the lithium-ion battery, which powers everything from the smallest personal electronics to gargantuan energy storage systems, has been nothing short of revolutionary. But as anyone who’s boarded a plane in the last decade could tell you, storing and pumping out energy
items.content:
The rise of the lithium-ion battery, which powers everything from the smallest personal electronics to gargantuan energy storage systems, has been nothing short of revolutionary. But as anyone who’s boarded a plane in the last decade could tell you, storing and pumping out energy by moving charged lithium ions through a liquid electrolyte soup has its drawbacks, not least that the batteries have a troubling tendency to catch fire. Enter the solid-state battery, which swaps liquid for a solid ceramic or polymer, creating power packs that charge faster, last longer, cram more energy into smaller spaces, and (crucially) run cooler. A new generation of companies aim to bring such batteries to market, and if their bets pan out, the tech could substantially ease the shift away from fossil fuels.

Solid-state batteries have been “just a few years away” for more than a decade now. In laboratories, the technology works. But there have been challenges. In designs that pair the solid electrolyte with a lithium-metal anode (the side of the battery that releases electrons into an electrical circuit), needlelike filaments called dendrites tend to grow during charging, and they eventually push through the electrolyte and short the cell. Solid electrolytes are supposed to physically block the formation of dendrites, but many of them crack as the treelike projections break through like roots in a concrete foundation.

Then there’s the problem of manufacturing at scale. Mass production requires large quantities of defect-free sheets of ceramic-like material to make the electrolytes as well as dry rooms for assembly, since those electrolytes have a tendency to react with water. Would-be manufacturers quote a range of potential prices for solid-state batteries, but most expect them to fall in line with lithium-ion packs sometime in the mid-2030s.

Nascent as the technology is, solid-state batteries have already seen high-­profile missteps . But one of America’s most advanced solid-state-battery companies says it’s closing in on being able to bring its product to market. The Bill Gates–backed QuantumScape launched in Silicon Valley in 2010 and built its battery around a class of ceramic materials that it says is compatible with lithium—meaning no dendrite formation. “We spent, then, like 10 years learning how to process it to satisfy all of the other requirements,” says Tim Holme, QuantumScape’s cofounder and chief technology officer. In 2025, the startup announced a proprietary, large-scale manufacturing method for quickly producing and heat-treating the ceramic electrolytes used in its batteries. “Nobody has ever done this in the field of ceramics before,” Holme claims. For 10,000 years, producing ceramics has involved slowly cooking the starting materials in an oven over the course of days. “We figured out a way to shorten that down to several minutes,” he says.

Plenty of other companies are pushing the tech forward as well. Toyota, the world’s biggest automaker, launched a research program on solid-state batteries way back in 2010. It’s now partnering with the global energy and petroleum company Idemitsu Kosan on a pilot plant, promising cars that can travel up to 745 miles after charging 10 minutes or less—a huge leap, if it works out. In China, CATL, the giant behind roughly 40% of the global battery market, is aggressively pursuing solid-state batteries too, pumping nearly $2.6 billion into a research program in 2024 alone. Mercedes, meanwhile, equipped one of its EQS sedans with solid-state batteries last fall; after driving nonstop for 750 miles, the car still had some range to spare.

Will the tech gain traction? Investing in vehicle batteries makes sense given the size of the potential market. But any little uptick in cost typically gets passed on to buyers, so the first solid-state EV batteries will inevitably be more expensive.

Grid storage buyers, who are working to meet the increasing demands posed by data centers, may also hesitate to purchase new technologies that still haven’t come down the cost curve. Then again, the promise of energy storage that lasts longer than lithium-­ion’s typical eight hours could make them easier to persuade.

Some companies are taking a page from a playbook employed by outfits pursuing fusion: Focus on near-term markets with better margins to help fund development and bring down costs. Solid-state firms including California-based Solid Energies and Arizona-headquartered Sion Power are looking at selling batteries to the aviation industry or the military. “Those are sectors that are less sensitive to cost, and they typically require lower volumes as well,” says Evelina Stoikou, head analyst for battery technologies and supply chains at the consultancy BloombergNEF. “It’s a good way to prove your concept, then go through and fund the pilot plant where you can make that and eventually scale up.”

The technology works, the capital is there, and demand is not far behind. But as with anything in manufacturing, unknown unknowns remain.

items.content:
오픈AI가 '챗GPT'의 개인정보 보호 기능을 강화하고 민감한 대화에 대한 접근을 제한하는 새로운 기능을 선보였다. 대화 기록과 메모리를 일반 채팅과 분리해 사적인 정보가 노출될 가능성을 줄이는 데 초점을 맞췄다.

오픈AI는 20일(현지시간) 챗GPT에서 민감한 대화를 별도로 보호할 수 있는 '채팅 잠금(Locked Chats)' 기능을 도입했다.

사용자가 다른 사람에게 기기를 보여주거나 화면을 공유할 때 사적인 대화가 노출되는 것을 막기 위한 기능이다.

잠금 기능을 적용한 대화는 일반 채팅 기록과 검색 결과에서 사라지고, 별도의 '잠긴 채팅(Locked chats)' 섹션에 보관된다. 웹과 데스크톱에서는 4자리 PIN으로 잠금을 해제할 수 있으며, 지원되는 모바일 기기에서는 페이스ID와 터치ID, 기기 잠금 해제 방식도 사용할 수 있다.

일반적인 대화 기록과 메모리 기능도 분리된다. 메모리 기능이 활성화되면 잠긴 대화에서 새로 입력한 정보는 잠긴 채팅끼리 공유되는 별도 메모리에 반영되며, 일반 대화의 메모리에는 업데이트되지 않는다. 다만 잠금 설정 이전에 챗GPT가 이미 기억한 정보까지 삭제되는 것은 아니다.

Keep sensitive conversations out of view with Locked Chats in ChatGPT.

Move chats out of your regular history and search into a protected space you can unlock with a PIN on web and desktop, or a PIN, Face ID, Touch ID, or device unlock on supported mobile devices.

New messages… pic.twitter.com/tV0wBj8f0i

이번 기능은 일시적인 대화(Temporary Chat)와 달리 대화를 기록으로 남겨두면서 접근을 제한하는 방식이다. 일시적인 대화는 일반 기록에 저장되지 않지만, 잠긴 채팅은 사용자가 언제든 다시 열어 이어갈 수 있다.

다만 채팅 잠금이 종단간 암호화나 별도의 암호화 저장소를 제공하는 것은 아니다. 대화 보관 기간이나 모델 개선 설정도 바뀌지 않는다. 따라서 민감한 대화에 대한 접근을 제한하는 기능이지, 저장된 데이터의 처리 방식 자체를 변경하는 보안 기능은 아니다.

PIN을 재설정할 때는 주의가 필요하다. 기존 PIN을 재설정하면 잠긴 대화와 해당 대화에만 저장된 기억, 보호된 파일 등이 영구 삭제되며 복구할 수 없다. 잠긴 대화는 그룹 채팅과 보관된 대화, 일시적인 대화, 예약 작업이나 회의 녹음이 연결된 대화 등 일부 유형에서는 사용할 수 없다.

오픈AI는 이번 기능을 무료 요금제와 고, 플러스, 프로, 비즈니스, 엔터프라이즈, 에듀 사용자에게 차례로 배포하기 시작했다. 다만 헬스케어용 챗GPT에서는 제공되지 않는다.
