items.content:
광양시육아종합지원센터에서 유아와 보호자를 위한 가족 문화공연 ‘샌드매직쇼’가 열렸다.

광양은 지난 17일 육아종합지원센터 대강당에서 유아와 보호자 등 200여명이 참여한 가운데 공연을 2차례 진행했다고 21일 밝혔다.

공연은 오후 2시와 4시로 나눠 진행됐으며 회당 100여명이 관람했다.

프로그램은 샌드아트와 코믹 키즈 매직쇼로 구성됐다. 샌드아트 공연에서는 동화 ‘아낌없이 주는 나무’를 모래 그림과 캐릭터로 표현했다.

이어진 마술공연에서는 어린이 참여형 마술과 공중부양 마술, 풍선 퍼포먼스 등을 선보였다. 일부 어린이들은 직접 무대에 올라 공연에 참여했다.

광양시육아종합지원센터는 올해 5월과 10월 두 차례 가족 문화공연을 운영했으며, 오는 11월과 12월에도 각각 한 차례씩 추가 공연을 진행할 예정이다.

광양시육아종합지원센터 관계자는 “앞으로도 영유아와 가족이 일상에서 문화예술을 접할 수 있도록 공연과 체험 프로그램을 지속적으로 운영하겠다”며 “아이들의 건강한 성장과 가족의 행복을 지원하는 데 힘쓰겠다”고 말했다.

items.content:
광주에서 도시농업을 직접 체험할 수 있는 ‘2026 광주 도시농부 축제’가 열린다.

전남광주통합특별시는 오는 23일부터 25일까지 광주청사 잔디광장 일원에서 ‘누구나 시작하는 도시농업…오늘, 도시에서 농부할래?’를 주제로 축제를 개최한다고 21일 밝혔다.

행사에는 한국원예치료복지협회 광주특별시지회를 비롯해 마스터가드너, 치유농업협회, 청년농업인 단체, 지역대학과 관련 기관·단체 등이 참여한다.

행사장에서는 도시농업 홍보 전시와 함께 반려식물 만들기, 허브미스트 만들기, 손수건 염색 등 체험 프로그램을 운영한다.

도시농업 전문가와의 1대1 맞춤교육을 통해 텃밭과 식물 관리 등 일상에서 활용할 수 있는 도시농업 정보도 제공한다.

어린이집을 대상으로는 상추 화분을 직접 만드는 ‘어린이 도시농부학교’를 운영한다. 지역대학과 연계한 기후위기 체험과 중앙아시아 다문화가정 프리마켓, 헤나 염색 체험도 마련된다.

24일과 25일에는 도시농업의 치유기능과 텃밭정원 치유 프로그램, 도시농업의 미래, 도시농업형 치유정원 등을 주제로 세미나가 진행된다. 도시농부들의 농악놀이와 추수감사 음악회 등 공연 프로그램도 운영한다.

이번 행사는 같은 기간 열리는 광주김치축제와 연계해 진행된다.

배귀숙 도시농업과장은 “이번 축제는 도시텃밭을 비롯해 치유농업, 반려식물 등 도시농업의 다양한 영역을 아우르는 체험과 전시, 세미나 등을 준비했다”며 “시민들이 축제에서 농업의 가치와 지속가능한 환경의 중요성, 지역 공동체 간 화합을 느끼는 계기가 되길 바란다”고 말했다.

items.content:
전남광주경제자유구역청이 미래모빌리티 산업 관련 기업을 대상으로 투자유치와 지역기업 판로 확대에 나선다.

전남광주경자청은 광주미래차모빌리티진흥원과 함께 21일부터 24일까지 대구 엑스코에서 열리는 ‘2026 대한민국 미래모빌리티 엑스포’에 참가해 공동홍보관을 운영한다고 21일 밝혔다.

행사에서는 전기·수소차를 비롯해 자율주행, 도심항공교통(UAM), 소프트웨어 중심 자동차(SDV), 이차전지와 자동차부품 등 미래차 관련 기술과 제품이 전시된다.

지역 모빌리티 기업 10곳의 주력 제품과 신기술도 전시해 투자자와 바이어를 대상으로 기업·산업 정보를 제공할 예정이다.

행사 기간에는 투자상담 부스도 운영한다. 모빌리티 관련 기업을 대상으로 전남광주경제자유구역의 입지와 기반시설을 안내하고 기업별 1대1 투자상담을 진행한다.

선석기 전남광주경제자유구역청장은 “이번 엑스포를 통해 전남광주의 차별화된 투자환경과 미래 모빌리티 산업 기반을 국내외에 널리 알릴 계획”이라며 “앞으로도 유망 모빌리티 기업들과 접점을 넓혀 실질적인 투자 유치로 이어질 수 있도록 최선을 다하겠다”고 밝혔다.

items.content:
AI 모델 경쟁이 성능뿐 아니라 응답 속도와 비용 효율성으로 확대되는 가운데, 확산 대형언어모델(dLLM)이 기존 모델의 한계를 넘어설 수 있다는 가능성을 보여주는 사례가 등장했다. 초고속 생성 능력에 더해 오픈AI와 앤트로픽의 모델에 버금가는 성능을 입증하며 복잡한 AI 에이전트 작업까지 겨냥했다.

인셉션(Inception)은 19일(현지시간) 초당 1000토큰 이상을 생성하면서도 'GPT-6 루나'와 '클로드 하이쿠 5.5'보다 높은 품질을 내세운 dLLM '머큐리 3(Mercury 3)'를 출시했다. 모델 규모를 이전 세대보다 40배 이상 키우고도 빠른 속도를 유지한 것이 특징이다.

"지금까지 출시된 dLLM 가운데 가장 강력하고 지능적인 모델"이라고 소개했다. 자체 벤치마크 결과를 기준으로 GPT-6 루나와 하이쿠 5.5보다 높은 품질을 보이면서 초당 1000토큰 이상의 생성 속도를 구현했다는 설명이다. 엔비디아 GPU 환경에서 측정한 생성 속도는 초당 1068토큰이다.

핵심 기술은 텍스트를 차례로 생성하는 대신 여러 위치의 토큰을 병렬로 다듬는 확산 방식이다. 기존 자기회귀(autoregressive) 모델은 앞선 토큰이 생성돼야 다음 토큰을 만들 수 있지만, 확산 모델(diffusion model)은 전체 답변의 초안을 만든 뒤 여러 단계에 걸쳐 동시에 개선한다. 순차 처리 단계를 줄여 응답 지연을 낮출 수 있다.

머큐리 3가 확산 모델도 규모를 키우면 지능을 높일 수 있다는 점을 보여준다고 강조했다. 첫 번째 모델인 '머큐리 1 미니'보다 전체 매개변수 규모를 40배 이상 늘렸으며, 두 모델 간 표준 벤치마크 평균 성능은 약 3배 향상됐다고 밝혔다. 다만 구체적인 매개변수 수는 공개하지 않았다.

이번 출시가 AI 성능을 높이면서도 지연 시간과 비용 부담을 줄일 수 있는 새로운 방법이라고 강조했다. "확산 모델은 지능이 비례적인 지연 시간 증가 없이 성장할 수 있는 새로운 길을 연다"고 밝혔다.

자체 벤치마크에서는 코딩과 지시 이행 분야에서 강점을 보였다. 'SWE-벤치 아틀라스' 점수는 51.08로, GPT-6 루나의 33.33과 하이쿠 5.5의 32.26을 웃돌았다. 'IF벤치'에서도 76.84점을 기록해 GPT-6 루나보다 약 15점 높았다. 'GPQA 다이아몬드' 점수는 89.23이었다.

모든 항목에서 경쟁 모델을 앞선 것은 아니다. '딥SWE v1'에서는 하이쿠 5.5가 51.62점으로 머큐리 3의 46.31점을 앞섰다. 긴 문맥에서 정보를 검색하는 'MRCR v2'에서도 하이쿠 5.5가 우위를 보였다. 일부 장문 검색과 복잡한 코딩 작업에서는 개선 여지가 남아 있는 셈이다.

머큐리 3는 코드 리뷰와 대화형 교육, 웹 탐색, 실시간 검색, 고객 지원 등 응답 속도가 중요한 AI 에이전트에 활용할 수 있다. 에이전트는 작업을 수행하는 과정에서 모델에 여러 차례 요청을 보내기 때문에 단계별 지연이 누적되기 쉽다. 빠른 응답을 제공하면 웹 탐색이나 문서 분석을 더 신속하게 진행하고, 제한된 시간 안에 여러 접근 방식을 시도할 수 있다는 설명이다.

얼리 액세스 파트너들도 다양한 활용 사례를 제시했다. 웹 탐색 자동화 업체 타이니피시(TinyFish)는 실제 웹 탐색 작업 50건 가운데 머큐리 3가 50%를 완료했다고 밝혔다. 옥텐 AI(Octen AI)는 스마트 안경 기반 검색에서 중앙값 기준 생성 시간이 0.9초, 전체 응답 시간이 2.2초였다고 전했다. 리비전두조(RevisionDojo)는 학습용 힌트와 답안 표시 기능이 약 1초 만에 제공된다고 설명했다.

이 모델은 인셉션 API 플랫폼과 오픈라우터, 베이스텐, 버셀 등을 통해 이용할 수 있다. 오픈AI API와 호환돼 기존 개발 환경에 비교적 쉽게 통합할 수 있으며, 최대 100만 토큰의 문맥 길이를 지원한다.

정식 가격은 입력 토큰 100만개당 0.20달러, 출력 토큰 100만개당 0.70달러다. 출시 기념으로 50% 할인된 입력 0.10달러, 출력 0.35달러에 제공하며, 캐시된 입력 토큰은 입력 가격에서 90% 할인한다. 기업용 고객에게는 전용 처리 용량과 자동 확장, 데이터 보존 설정 등 추가 기능도 지원한다.

인셉션은 음성 AI의 첫 응답 지연을 줄이는 '머큐리 보이스(Mercury Voice)'와 대량 분류 작업에 특화한 의사결정 모델 '머큐리 디사이드(Mercury Decide)'도 함께 선보이며 실시간 AI 제품군을 확대하고 있다.

items.title: Europe Wants Data Centers. Its Climate Goals Are Getting in the Way
items.summary: A plan to funnel the heat given off by data centers into nearby homes has run aground in Germany. Across Europe, policymakers are weighing AI ambitions against climate objectives.
items.content:
Earlier this year, the German government laid out an ambitious plan : By 2030, it would double the scale of the country’s data center fleet, and quadruple the amount of compute available for running artificial intelligence models. The idea was to minimize Germany’s dependence on the United States for access to AI—a point of concern across Europe —and boost its faltering economy.

However, Germany has found that its AI ambitions are butting up against its climate commitments. EU member states have committed to cutting greenhouse gas emissions by 55 percent by the end of the decade. But policies meant to help meet that target are interfering with attempts to trigger a data center building frenzy.

As part of its broader climate commitments, the previous German administration voted through the Energy Efficiency Act in 2023. Among other things, it required all new data centers to recycle a portion of the waste heat generated by their computer equipment, ideally into nearby municipal heating systems. It seemed like a no-brainer, says Patrick Graichen, who served as a senior official at Germany’s Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy at the time, before resigning over cronyism allegations.

“We need clean heat, and data centers are a source of clean heat,” Graichen tells WIRED.

In June, a month before the rules were due to finally take effect, the German federal government walked them back . Data center firms had complained that the requirements made it almost impossible to build in the country; the German Data Center Association characterized an early version of the bill as a “ data center prevention act .” Under an amended bill, which will be put to the German parliament for ratification imminently, data center operators would no longer be obligated to reuse waste heat, only to scope out the possibility.

Graichen and others have accused the German government of sacrificing climate targets for a chance to ride the AI wave. But countries across Europe find themselves pulled between these same two poles, under simultaneous pressure to cash in on rapid growth in the energy-intensive AI sector—and limit dependence on the US—and to protect the climate.

The German Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy did not respond to a request for comment.

Among data center developers, the chief objection to the original Energy Efficiency Act was the chance it could land them in an impossible bind, obligated to reuse waste heat even when there was no available offtake—whether a municipal heating system or an industry, like greenhouse agriculture. “Some of the things they had to comply with were outside of their control,” says Barbara Smitten, associate director for critical systems at consulting firm Cundall. “It felt that [the burden] was all on the data center.”

In the last 18 months, multiple data center proposals have fallen through in Germany: Stack Infrastructure canceled a $3 billion facility in Hesse, and state-owned Komm.ONE withdrew from a project in Baden-Württemberg. Though precisely what causes a data center development to fold is rarely clear, Komm.ONE pointed directly to the burdens of the Energy Efficiency Act.

Graichen claims that the industry’s objections are groundless. He says the availability of a heat offtake should become a default criterion for any developer searching for a new site. “Stop complaining,” he says.

When an offtake is available, recycling heat produced by a data center is straightforward. “There is no technical reason why a data center cannot use its waste heat. The technologies and concepts are well known,” says John Booth, managing director at IT consultancy Carbon3IT, who helped to devise EU-wide energy efficiency targets for data centers. “There is absolutely no reason except the will of the organization to do it.”

Nevertheless, under the amended Energy Efficiency Act, data center developers are required only to assess whether recycling heat is economically and technically feasible. If not, they are exempt. “With practical rules for data centers, we are creating the conditions for digital sovereignty and economic growth,” wrote Katherina Reiche, federal minister for economic affairs and energy, when the cabinet approved the change.

The amendment may unlock pent-up demand among data center developers to build in Germany, whose geographic centrality makes it easy to route data efficiently into Western and Eastern Europe. “It lessens the risk of people not seeing the German market as attractive,” says Smitten.

But in a roundabout way, it could also undermine the aim to spark a building frenzy, inviting the type of climate-focused activism that has led to permitting freezes and data center moratoria in the US. Already, in February, the city council of a small German town voted to block the construction of a $2.5 billion data center development, partly over climate concerns.

As policymakers contend with conflicting ambitions to improve domestic AI capabilities and meet climate objectives, some say the swelling public unease about that trade-off will complicate things yet further in Europe. In the last year, the attitude toward data centers “has switched completely,” claims Graichen. “First and foremost in the US, but the same will happen in Europe.”

items.content:
아마존에 이어 구글도 기존 AI 개발 도구를 자체 칩에서 손쉽게 사용할 수 있도록 소프트웨어 생태계 확장에 나섰다. 개발자들이 익숙한 파이토치(PyTorch) 코드를 큰 수정 없이 자체 칩으로 옮길 수 있도록 지원해, 엔비디아 GPU와 CUDA 중심의 개발 환경에서 하드웨어 선택지를 넓히려는 움직임이다.

구글은 20일(현지시간) 열린 '파이토치 컨퍼런스 2026'에서 TPU용 파이토치 소프트웨어 스택인 ' 토치TPU(TorchTPU) '를 오픈소스로 공개했다.

아마존도 전날 자체 AI 칩 트레이니엄(Trainium)에서 기존 파이토치 코드를 실행하는 ‘토치뉴런(TorchNeuron)’을 발표했다. 아마존은 설정 하나를 바꾸는 방식으로 코드를 다시 작성하지 않고도 트레이니엄을 사용할 수 있다고 설명했으며, 20일부터 공개 베타로 제공한다.

파이토치는 AI 모델 개발과 학습에 널리 쓰이는 오픈소스 프레임워크다. 그동안 엔비디아 GPU와 CUDA에 맞춰 구축한 코드와 도구가 많아 다른 칩으로 옮기려면 추가 작업이 필요했다. 두 회사는 이 전환 부담을 줄여 자체 칩의 활용 폭을 넓히겠다는 것이다.

메타의 파이토치 개발팀과 공동 개발한 토치TPU는 기존 파이토치 API를 유지하면서 TPU에서 모델 학습과 추론, 배포를 지원한다. 개발자는 최소한의 코드 변경으로 기존 애플리케이션을 TPU에서 실행할 수 있다.

일반 실행 모드에서 모델 오류를 확인한 뒤 ‘torch.compile’을 활용해 성능을 최적화할 수 있으며, 분산 학습 기능과 진단 도구도 기본 지원한다.

구글은 모델 실행뿐 아니라 학습과 추론에 쓰이는 주요 도구까지 TPU에 연결했다. 허깅페이스와 협력해 트랜스포머스(Transformers) v5에서 ‘device_map="tpu"’ 설정으로 모델을 TPU에 배치할 수 있도록 했다.

이미지 생성 모델 개발 도구인 디퓨저스(Diffusers)도 TPU에서 일반 실행 모드와 컴파일 최적화, 여러 칩에 모델을 나눠 실행하는 텐서 병렬 처리를 지원한다. 허깅페이스 모델을 TPU 인프라에서 지속적으로 테스트하는 체계도 구축했다.

대규모 모델 추론 도구인 ‘vLLM’과 ‘SGLang’의 TPU 지원도 강화했다. 인퍼랙트(Inferact), 라딕스아크(RadixArk)와 각각 협력해 TPU용 백엔드를 마련했으며, 기존 스케줄러와 API 서버 등은 유지하면서 TPU에 맞춰 연산을 최적화하도록 했다.

여러 서버에 추론 작업을 배분하는 쿠버네티스 기반 시스템 ‘llm-d’도 1.0 버전으로 공개했다. 요청 처리에 필요한 문맥이 이미 저장된 서버로 작업을 보내고, 입력을 처리하는 프리필(prefill)과 답변을 생성하는 디코딩(decode)을 분리해 효율을 높인다. 구글 클라우드의 쿠버네티스 엔진(GKE)에서는 공통 인터페이스로 GPU와 TPU를 활용할 수 있다.

학습 분야에서는 대규모 분산 학습 프레임워크 ‘토치타이탄(TorchTitan)’에 TPU 지원을 통합했다. 구글은 ‘큐원 3 8B’ 모델 학습에서 칩의 이론상 연산 성능을 실제 학습에 얼마나 활용하는지 나타내는 모델 연산 활용률(MFU)이 최대 52%를 기록했다고 밝혔다. 또 ‘아이언우드(Ironwood)’ TPU를 8192개까지 늘렸을 때 칩 수 증가에 거의 비례하는 성능 향상을 확인했다고 설명했다.

강화학습 프레임워크 ‘VeRL’에도 TPU 백엔드와 참고용 학습 구성을 추가했다. ‘레이(Ray)’를 통해서는 데이터 처리와 학습, 강화학습, 추론 등 단계별로 CPU와 GPU, TPU를 배정해 하나의 작업 흐름에서 함께 사용할 수 있도록 했다.

개발자의 이전 작업을 돕는 'TPU 에이전트 스위트(TPU Agent Suite)'도 깃허브 에서 프리뷰 버전으로 제공한다. 이 도구는 플러그인 방식으로 개발 환경에 연결해 초기 설정과 오류 진단, 사용 관련 질문, 추론 성능 조정을 지원한다.

이와 함께 온디바이스 AI 추론 도구 ‘라이트RT(LiteRT)’와 파이토치 모델을 연결하는 ‘라이트RT-토치(LiteRT-Torch)’도 공개했다. 파이토치 모델을 변환해 안드로이드와 iOS, 윈도, 맥OS, 리눅스, 웹, 사물인터넷(IoT) 기기에서 실행하도록 지원하며, 기기의 CPU와 GPU, 신경망처리장치(NPU)를 활용할 수 있다.

items.content:
얼굴 사진 한 장으로 암 환자의 생존 위험을 예측하는 AI 연구 결과가 나왔다. 얼굴이 얼마나 늙어 보이는지 측정한 뒤 건강 상태를 추정하던 방식에서 나아가, 환자의 사진과 실제 생존 기록을 연결해 사망 위험을 직접 학습한 것이 특징이다.

매사추세츠 종합 브리검과 다나-파버 암 연구소, 하버드 의과대학 등 연구진은 19일(현지시간) 국제 학술지 ‘랜싯 디지털 헬스’에 얼굴 사진을 활용한 건강 평가 기반 모델 ‘ FAHR-페이스(FAHR-Face) ’의 개발·검증 결과를 발표했다.

연구진은 4000만장 이상의 얼굴 이미지로 기반 모델을 학습한 뒤, 이를 생물학적 나이 추정 도구 ‘FAHR-페이스에이지’와 암 환자 생존 위험 예측 도구 ‘FAHR-페이스서바이벌’로 각각 발전시켰다.

생존 예측 모델의 추가 학습에는 암 환자 사진 3만4389장을 사용했으며, 별도의 암 환자 데이터로 예측 성능을 검증했다.

얼굴 사진으로 나이나 피부 상태를 분석하는 서비스는 이미 나와 있다. 예를 들어 노보스(NOVOS)의 ‘페이스에이지’는 얼굴 전체와 눈 주변의 외관상 나이를 추정한다. 회사는 이 결과가 눈에 보이는 노화 징후를 분석한 값이며 생물학적 나이를 측정한 것은 아니라고 설명한다.

얼굴과 건강 상태를 연결한 연구도 처음은 아니다. 같은 연구팀은 지난해 5월 ‘페이스에이지’ 연구를 발표했다. 건강한 사람 5만8851명의 데이터로 모델을 학습하고 암 환자 6196명을 대상으로 평가한 결과, 얼굴 나이가 높을수록 생존 전망이 나빠지는 연관성을 확인했다.

이번 연구의 차이는 학습 규모 확대와 예측 목표에 있다. 기존 페이스에이지가 얼굴에서 추정한 나이를 생존 전망과 연결했다면, 페이스서바이벌은 환자의 생존 기록을 직접 학습한다.

또 대규모 얼굴 이미지로 공통 특징을 익힌 기반 모델을 만들어, 나이 추정과 생존 예측 등 서로 다른 작업에 활용했다. 연구진은 이를 통해 건강 지표마다 모델을 처음부터 개발해야 하는 부담을 줄일 수 있다고 설명했다.

두 도구가 주목한 얼굴 부위도 달랐다. 페이스에이지는 팔자주름과 이마, 관자놀이에, 페이스서바이벌은 눈 밑과 콧대 주변에 주로 반응했다.

두 예측값의 상관관계는 약했으며, 함께 활용했을 때 외부 검증 데이터에서 실제 생존 결과를 설명하는 데 도움이 됐다. 즉, 얼굴의 노화 정도와 생존 위험에서 서로 보완적인 정보를 얻었다는 설명이다.

다만 AI가 해당 부위에서 어떤 건강 신호를 포착했는지, 그것이 사망 위험과 어떻게 연결되는지까지 밝혀진 것은 아니다.

연구진이 밝힌 용도는 환자가 강도 높은 치료를 견딜 수 있을지 판단하는 일을 돕는 것이다. 같은 나이와 진단을 가진 환자라도 체력과 회복 능력이 다르기 때문에, 수술이나 방사선 치료를 결정할 때 이를 평가할 추가 지표가 필요하다는 취지다.

그러나 사진으로 개인의 남은 수명을 정확히 알아내거나, 이 결과만으로 치료 방침을 정할 수 있는 단계는 아니다. 연구진은 BBC 인터뷰에서 다양한 인종의 얼굴과 더 많은 데이터를 확보해 검증해야 한다고 밝혔다.

영국 서리대학교의 미로슬라프 보버 교수도 병원과 환자 집단을 달리한 평가, 의사의 판단과 비교하는 검증이 필요하다며 아직 임상에 사용할 준비가 되지 않았다고 평가했다.

items.content:
AI 비디오 생성 시장에서 품질 경쟁에 이어 속도 경쟁이 본격화하고 있다. 고품질 영상을 수초 만에 제작할 수 있는 기술이 등장하면서 기업의 콘텐츠 제작 방식에도 변화가 예상된다.

기업용 AI 멀티미디어 제작 플랫폼 팔(fal)은 20일(현지시간) 독일 AI 모델 개발사 블랙 포레스트 랩스(Black Forest Labs)와 공동 개발한 비디오 생성 모델 '플럭스 3 맥스(FLUX 3 Max)'를 출시했다.

특히 이번 모델은 사용자 맞춤형(Customization)에 중점을 두고 설계된 것이 특징이다.

또 10초 분량의 영상을 약 12초 만에 생성하는 등 속도를 강조했다. 이는 경쟁 모델인 바이트댄스의 '시댄스 2.5(Seedance 2.5)'보다 약 22배 빠른 속도다.

Introducing FLUX 3 Max.

Fastest in the west. Fast enough to try anything. And everything.

Generate a 10-second video in 12 seconds.

Tied for #1 in image-to-video. 22× faster than Seedance 2.5 at the same quality.

FLUX 3 is a model designed for customization. @fal adapted and… pic.twitter.com/o1Q0nkB8A1

fal이 공개한 비교 결과에 따르면 플럭스 3 맥스는 10초 분량의 영상을 생성하는 데 평균 12.45초가 걸렸다. 시댄스 2.5는 같은 작업에 277.80초가 소요됐다. fal이 제시한 벤치마크에서는 두 모델이 동일한 품질 점수를 기록했다.

사후 학습과 추론 최적화 기술을 적용한 결과물로 소개했다. 기존 '플럭스 3 비디오(FLUX 3 Video)' 모델을 기반으로 영상 품질을 개선하면서 생성 속도도 높였다는 것이다. "플럭스 3의 품질을 50 Elo 포인트 높이는 동시에 영상 생성 속도를 11.5배 개선했다"고 밝혔다.

실사에 가까운 표현과 자연스러운 움직임, 영화 같은 조명, 세밀한 질감 구현을 주요 강점으로 내세웠다. 블랙 포레스트 랩스는 음성 표현과 물리적으로 설득력 있는 동작, 음향 효과, 독창적인 장면 생성 등도 강조했다.

아티피셜 애널리시스 벤치마크 기준 플럭스 3 맥스는 1139 Elo를 기록해 시댄스 2.5와 동등한 수준의 선두권 품질을 기록했다. 다만 미니맥스 'H3'가 1124점으로 뒤를 잇는 등 평가 결과의 불확실성 범위가 겹쳐 선두권 모델 사이의 품질 우열을 명확하게 가리기는 어렵다. 또 해당 평가는 '이미지 기반 생성(Image-to-Video)'에 국한된 선호도 측정인 만큼, 전체 성능이나 텍스트 기반 생성 작업 전반을 단정하기는 이르다.

플럭스 3 맥스는 '텍스트-투-비디오(Text-to-Video)'와 '이미지-투-비디오' 기능을 모두 지원한다. 텍스트 기반 생성은 설명문을 입력해 영상을 만들며, 이미지 기반 생성은 시작 이미지를 활용한다. 이미지 기반 작업에서는 종료 이미지도 지정할 수 있다. 최대 10장의 이미지를 영상의 주요 시점에 배치하는 키프레임(Keyframes) 방식도 제공해 장면 전개를 세밀하게 제어할 수 있다.

생성 가능한 영상 길이는 5~20초이며, 기본 해상도는 720p다. 필요에 따라 1080p로 업스케일링할 수 있고, 가로형·세로형·정사각형 화면 비율도 지원한다. 음성 생성 기능은 사용자가 켜거나 끌 수 있다.

가격 경쟁력도 내세웠다. 출시 후 3주 동안 75% 할인된 가격에 제공한다.

정규 API 요금은 720p 기준 초당 0.17달러, 1080p 기준 초당 0.29달러다. 이를 적용하면 10초 영상 한 편의 생성 비용은 각각 1.70달러와 2.90달러다.

또 API를 통해 생성한 콘텐츠는 이용 약관에 따라 상업적으로 활용할 수 있다고 안내했다.

items.title: 로봇 양반 갈 때도 아주 예술로 가는구만
[게시판] 플렉스, 한국MS와 기업용 AI 협력 등 단신

items.content:
■ 플렉스(대표 장해남)는 한국마이크로소프트와 국내 기업의 AI 전환(AX) 가속화를 위한 업무협약(MOU)을 체결했다고 밝혔다. 양사는 국내 기업 대상 공동 영업과 제품·기술 연동, 상호 솔루션 적용 검토 등 세 가지 분야에서 협력한다. 플렉스는 자사의 조직·인재 데이터를 마이크로소프트 365 코파일럿과 연계해 질문자의 직무와 조직 내 맥락을 반영해 답하는 기업용 AI를 구현할 계획이다.

■ 코난테크놀로지(대표 김영섬)는 서울과학기술대학교(서울과기대)와 국방 AI 분야 공동연구 및 전문인재 양성을 위한 업무협약(MOU)을 체결했다고 밝혔다. 양 기관은 정부과제 공동 수행과 인턴십 연계, 실무 교육 등을 추진한다. 코난테크놀로지는 AI 기반 정보감시정찰(ISR) 등 국방 AI 솔루션 개발을, 서울과기대는 교원 자문과 공동연구를 맡는다.

■ 이스트소프트(대표 정상원)는 제주국제자유도시개발센터(JDC)의 '사내 생성형 AI 언어모델(sLLM) 구축 사업'의 수행 기업으로 선정됐다고 밝혔다. 외부망과 분리된 내부 서버에 sLLM과 AI 에이전트를 결합한 업무지원 플랫폼을 구축한다. 개발사업과 면세사업, 예산 등 업무 영역별 특화 챗봇과 약 3.8테라바이트(TB) 규모 내부 문서 기반 검색증강생성(RAG) 서비스도 제공할 예정이다.

■ 제논(대표 고석태)은 인도네시아 소재 나이키 신발 생산 공장에서 진행한 비전 AI 기반 아웃솔 검사 과제가 양산 검증을 통과했다고 밝혔다. 고해상도 카메라로 촬영한 제품 표면을 AI가 분석해 불량을 자동으로 판별하는 방식으로 최대 99.7%의 불량 탐지율을 기록했다. 내년 생산라인 투입을 목표로 양산 모델을 개발하며 신발 상판 불량 검사와 협동로봇 기반 공정 자동화 등으로 현지 사업을 확대할 예정이다.

■ 파일러(대표 오재호)는 자사 AI 팀의 논문 2편이 글로벌 AI 학술대회 '뉴립스(NeurIPS) 2026'에 채택됐다고 밝혔다. 채택된 논문은 목소리의 감정과 억양 등 비언어적 정보까지 AI가 이해하도록 돕는 ‘CoAT’와 오류가 포함된 데이터에서도 AI가 안정적으로 학습하도록 하는 ‘GAPO’다. 해당 기술은 파일러의 브랜드 세이프티와 콘텐츠 검수 등에 활용될 예정이다.

items.content:
메타의 AI 에이전트 앱 '뮤즈(Muse)'가 출시 40일 만에 미국에서 다운로드 1000만건을 돌파했다. 모바일 앱 가운데 출시 초기 이 같은 기록을 달성한 것은 역대 12번째로, 게임이 아닌 앱으로는 '디즈니플러스'와 메타의 '스레드'에 이어 세 번째다.

20일(현지시간) 시장조사업체 센서타워의 데이터에 따르면, 뮤즈는 지난 9월 출시 이후 전 세계에서 총 1090만건의 다운로드를 기록했다. 이 가운데 1020만건이 미국에서 발생했다.

센서타워의 카라 리 선임 인사이트 애널리스트는 출시 후 40일 만에 이 같은 성과를 낸 앱은 뮤즈를 포함해 지금까지 12개뿐이라고 밝혔다. 앞서 이 기록을 달성한 앱은 대부분 포트나이트, 배틀그라운드 모바일, 포켓몬 고 등 모바일 게임이었다. 비게임 앱 중에서는 2023년 7월 메타의 스레드가 가장 최근 사례였으며, 그 이전에는 디즈니플러스가 이름을 올렸다.

뮤즈의 빠른 성장에는 메타의 광범위한 서비스 생태계와 공격적인 마케팅이 영향을 미친 것으로 풀이된다. 페이스북과 인스타그램 등 일간 활성 사용자 수가 총 36억명에 달하는 자체 플랫폼을 활용해 뮤즈를 홍보하고 있다. 여기에 광고비까지 집중적으로 투입하며 사용자 확보에 속도를 내고 있다.

센서타워에 따르면 메타는 10월 전체 광고비의 39%를 뮤즈 마케팅에 배정했다. 지난달 23%에서 크게 늘어난 수치다. 미국 내 광고 노출 기준 브랜드 순위도 9월 73위에서 10월 21위로 뛰어올랐다.

다운로드 증가뿐 아니라 사용자 유지율에서도 경쟁 앱을 앞섰다. 미국 시장에서 출시 7일 차 잔존율은 30%, 14일 차는 23%로 집계됐다. 센서타워가 파악한 경쟁 AI 앱들의 평균 잔존율인 7일 차 19%, 14일 차 16%를 모두 웃돌았다.

실제 사용 규모도 확대되고 있다. 일간 활성 사용자(DAU)는 16일 처음으로 250만명을 넘어섰으며, 전주보다 15% 증가했다. 출시 이후 미국 애플 앱스토어에서 대부분 기간 1위를 유지했고, 구글 플레이에서도 최근 30일 동안 정상에 올랐다. 지난 19일에는 스트리밍 앱 '킥(Kick)'에 잠시 1위를 내줬지만 이후 다시 선두를 되찾았다.

경쟁 서비스와 비교하면 초기 성장세는 더 두드러진다. '챗GPT'는 출시 후 첫 40일 동안 미국에서 370만건의 다운로드를 기록했다. '그록'과 '클로드'는 각각 50만건, 20만건에 그쳤다. 다만 전 세계 다운로드 기준으로는 챗GPT가 같은 기간 1500만건을 기록해 뮤즈를 앞섰다.

두 앱의 성과를 단순 비교하기는 어렵다. 뮤즈는 현재 미국과 캐나다에서만 이용할 수 있지만, 챗GPT는 일본과 브라질, 독일 등 더 넓은 시장에서 출시 초기부터 사용자를 확보했다. 챗GPT의 첫 40일간 전 세계 다운로드 중 일본이 차지한 비중만 25%에 달했다.

items.content:
오픈AI가 신약 개발 과정을 관리하는 AI 스타트업 오케스트라 바이오(Orchestra Bio)를 인수했다. 생명과학 연구용 AI 모델과 도구를 제공하는 '로잘린드(Rosalind)'에 오케스트라의 기술과 인력을 결합해 신약 개발 전반을 지원하는 AI 에이전트 구축에 나선다.

오픈AI는 20일(현지시간) 오케스트라 바이오를 인수했다고 공식 발표했다. 인수 금액은 공개하지 않았다.

오케스트라는 바이오테크 기업이 신약 개발 과정에서 발생하는 복잡한 업무와 일정을 관리하도록 돕는 플랫폼을 개발해 왔다. 2025년까지 앤드리슨 호로위츠, 아트리아, 8VC 등으로부터 2000만달러(약 260억원)의 투자를 유치한 것으로 알려졌다.

이번 인수는 오픈AI의 생명과학 분야 사업을 강화하기 위한 조치다. 전문 인력과 기술을 로잘린드에 통합해 과학적 발견을 실제 치료제로 발전시키는 데 필요한 연구와 업무 조율을 지원할 계획이다.

신약 개발은 표적 발굴부터 규제 당국의 승인까지 미국에서 평균 10~15년이 걸릴 정도로 복잡하다. 과학적 연구뿐 아니라 임상시험과 제조, 일정 관리 등 여러 부서와 외부 파트너가 참여하는 업무도 조율해야 한다. 이 과정에서 서로 연결되지 않은 시스템을 사용하는 경우가 많아 정보 공유와 의사결정이 지연될 수 있다.

오케스트라의 플랫폼은 사람과 AI 에이전트가 협력해 신약 개발 프로그램을 관리하도록 설계됐다. 연구진과 프로젝트 책임자는 에이전트에 연구 진행 상황과 실험, 일정 등을 추적하는 업무를 맡기고 주요 의사결정과 문제 해결에 집중할 수 있다.

예를 들어 의약품 제조 과정에서 한 차례 문제가 발생하면 임상시험 시작 일정까지 영향받을 수 있다. 오케스트라의 AI 에이전트는 관련 활동과 일정을 파악하고 대응 방안을 비교해 연구진이 후속 조치를 결정하도록 지원한다. 단순한 정보 검색을 넘어 신약 개발 과정에서 발생하는 여러 업무의 연관성을 분석하고 실행을 조율하는 방식이다.

오픈AI의 로잘린드는 생물학과 화학 분야의 연구를 지원하는 AI 모델 'GPT-로잘린드'와 실험 계획 및 결과 분석을 돕는 '로잘린드 워크벤치'로 구성된다. 이번 인수를 통해 과학적 질문에 답하고 실험을 설계하는 기능에 더해, 연구 결과를 실제 개발 단계로 연결하는 업무 관리 역량까지 강화할 수 있을 것으로 기대하고 있다.

이미 제약업계와의 협력도 진행 중이다. 노보 노디스크와 협력해 연구개발과 상업화 과정의 효율성을 높이는 방안을 모색하고 있으며, 모더나에서도 복잡한 데이터를 분석해 실험 업무로 연결하는 데 AI를 활용하고 있다고 밝혔다.

최근 주요 AI 기업들은 산업별 전문 소프트웨어 시장으로 영역을 넓히고 있다. 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등은 이제 모델 제공을 넘어 제약·바이오 분야의 실제 업무에 직접 적용할 수 있는 도구와 에이전트를 개발하고 있다. 전문 스타트업 입장에서는 대형 AI 기업과의 경쟁이 부담될 수 있지만, 오케스트라 바이오는 인수 후 오픈AI의 생명과학 사업에 기술과 인력을 결합하는 방향을 택했다.

오픈AI는 "AI가 과학자들의 발견을 돕는 데 그치지 않고, 유망한 치료제를 발전시키는 데 필요한 업무까지 지원해 신약이 환자에게 더 빨리 도달하도록 하는 것이 목표"라고 밝혔다.

items.content:
중국이 국가 차원의 데이터 자원을 통합·운영하는 국영 기업을 출범시키며 AI 경쟁력 강화에 나섰다. 산업과 지역별로 흩어진 데이터를 연결하고 활용도를 높여 독자적인 AI 생태계와 디지털 경제 기반을 강화하려는 전략이다.

신화통신 등에 따르면, 중국은 20일 허베이성 슝안신구에서 중앙정부가 관리하는 국영 기업인 '국가데이터그룹(China National Data Group)' 출범식을 열었다.

딩쉐샹 중국 국무원 부총리가 참석해 출범을 공식화했다. 본사는 슝안신구에 두며, 데이터 자원의 개발과 활용을 핵심 사업으로 맡는다.

딩 부총리는 이번 설립이 "AI 발전의 기회를 선점하고 디지털 중국 건설을 가속하며 국가 경쟁에서 새로운 우위를 확보하는 데 중요한 의미가 있다"고 밝혔다. 이어 데이터 인프라 구축을 서두르고 핵심 기술 개발을 강화해 데이터 분야에서 전략적·선도적·지원적 역할을 해야 한다고 강조했다.

국가급 데이터 자원을 개발·통합·운영하고 산업과 지역 간 데이터 이동 및 공유를 촉진하는 역할을 맡는다. 데이터의 경제적 가치를 높이고 새로운 사업 모델을 발굴하는 한편, 정부 부처와 지방정부, 기업, 연구기관 간 협력을 통해 데이터 산업 생태계를 확대할 계획이다.

중국은 2023년 국가데이터국을 설립해 데이터 관련 정책과 제도 설계를 담당해 왔다. 이번에 출범한 국가데이터그룹은 정책 수립보다 실제 데이터 자원의 운영과 활용, 시장 확대 등 실행 업무에 무게를 둔다. 정책을 설계하는 행정 조직과 사업을 수행하는 국영 기업을 분리해 데이터 산업의 실행력을 높이려는 구조다.

전문가 자문위원회 위원인 장샹훙은 이 조직이 국가급 데이터 자원의 개발과 통합, 운영을 담당하게 될 것이라고 설명했다. 그는 산업과 지역을 넘나드는 데이터 공유가 확대되면 자원 배분의 효율성을 높이고, 개별 조직에 데이터가 고립되는 '데이터 사일로' 문제를 해소할 수 있다고 평가했다. 이를 통해 전국 단위의 통합 데이터 시장 구축도 앞당길 수 있다는 분석이다.

이번 조치는 AI 산업 육성을 위한 중국의 기술 자립 전략에 따른 것이다. AI 모델의 성능을 높이려면 고품질 데이터와 이를 처리할 컴퓨팅 인프라가 필수적이다. 미국의 첨단 반도체 수출 통제로 하드웨어 확보에 제약받는 상황에서 데이터 자원의 활용 효율을 높이는 것은 중국이 자체 AI 산업의 경쟁력을 강화하기 위한 주요 과제로 꼽힌다.

items.title: NVIDIA Kumo Forecast Combines Pretrained Time-Series Representations with Historical Pattern Retrieval and Interpretability
items.content:
NVIDIA Kumo Forecast (formerly known as NV-Tesseract Forecasting) is a multi-variate time-series forecasting model that combines a pretrained Transformer backbone with Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR), a context-enhanced forecasting mode that blends direct model predictions with patterns retrieved from historical data. This includes interpretability of the results. Built on the MOMENT-1-large backbone, Kumo Forecast uses an approximately 340-million-parameter base encoder plus a trainable forecasting head.

The library provides a DataFrame-first API, configurable forecast horizons, optional historical context for retrieval, and an interpretability framework that produces horizon-specific explanations without modifying the underlying forecaster.

Kumo-Forecast is available under Apache 2.0 license .

Model code: NVIDIA/Kumo-TS Model weights: nvidia/Kumo-Forecast

A forecasting system can draw on two different sources of information: representations learned during pretraining and historical observations available for the current application. Kumo-Forecast brings these together through a pretrained forecasting model and an optional retrieval pathway over historical context.

In its direct forecasting path, Kumo-Forecast uses a MOMENT-based Transformer and a trained forecasting head to predict future values. In Domain Aware Representation and Retrieval (DARR) mode, it also retrieves related patterns from historical data using a nearest-neighbor approach and combines that information with the direct forecast.

This creates a distinction between the model’s input window and its retrieval context. The input window supplies recent observations for the forecast; a separate historical DataFrame can supply additional context for pattern retrieval. Developers can adjust how strongly the final prediction relies on each pathway through the library’s configuration options.

Further information on DARR mode can be found in this published paper, Memory-Augmented Forecasting: Scalability and Generalization Across Temporal Domains

Kumo-Forecast combines four main components: a pretrained temporal encoder, a trainable forecasting head, historical-pattern retrieval mechanism and an interpretability framework.

Pretrained Temporal Representations : The model uses the MOMENT-1-large Transformer encoder as its backbone. The architecture keeps encoder and embedder weights frozen while training the forecasting head, separating the pretrained representation model from the task-specific prediction layer.

Direct Forecasting : The forecasting head maps the model’s representations to future values for the requested horizon. For horizons beyond the model’s native capability, there is support for autoregressive extension. This distinguishes a directly generated forecast from a longer forecast that extends predictions recursively.

Domain-Aware Representation and Retrieval : DARR augments direct forecasting with k-nearest-neighbor retrieval from historical context data. This process combines direct forecasts with historical-pattern retrieval, while the SDK accepts the historical context through a separate context_df argument.

Interpretability : Kumo-Forecasting also includes a model-agnostic interpretability framework. When enabled, it produces an explanation bundle containing lag and feature attributions per forecast horizon, semantic-flow diagnostics, trajectory-stability diagnostics, and optional embedding Integrated Gradients.These outputs accompany the forecast rather than requiring a different forecasting architecture.

Further details on interpretability can be found in this paper, NVExplain: Explaining Time Series Forecasting with Latent Trajectory Analysis and Structure-Preserving Surrogates

Data must be numeric, temporal data. Supported input sequence lengths include 256, 512, 1024, and 2048 observations. Inputs consist of a timestamp column and one or more numeric value columns, represented as a pandas DataFrame or a CSV/JSON input. When leveraging DARR mode, the dimensions of the context must be similar to the context of the input.

The Factory Operations (FOX) Blueprint includes Early Access to the Predictive Maintenance module which leverages Kumo Anomaly and Kumo Forecast. It analyzes real-time data to predict future anomalies. Your browser does not support the video tag.

For an application-specific evaluation, compare the direct and retrieval-enhanced configurations on the same held-out forecasting windows. Validate forecast quality across the intended horizons and operating conditions, consistent with NVIDIA’s requirement for use-case-specific testing

The Kumo-TS repository additionally provides an example for fine-tuning Kumo-Forecast on a user-supplied CSV. Developers therefore have both a pretrained inference workflow and a documented starting point for adapting the model to their own data.

items.title: The Future of CSS
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.joshwcomeau.com/css/interop-2027/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50175070 Points: 448 # Comments: 192
items.content:
For the past few years, all of the major browser vendors (Google, Apple, Microsoft, and Mozilla, along with Igalia and Bocoup) have been working together on Interop (opens in new tab) , a project to improve universal browser support on web technologies. It’s been a remarkably successful effort; when a focus area gets added to Interop, it often winds up reaching near-100% support across all major browsers within a year. ✨

CSS Subgrid is a good example. Subgrid is a super-powerful extension to CSS Grid which enables entirely new layouts . It was implemented in Firefox back in 2019, but there wasn’t much movement with other browsers for years. It got added to Interop 2023, and by the end of that year, it was widely available across all modern browsers:

As we reach the end of 2026, Interop 2027 is currently being planned, and the team at Mozilla has created a ranking system (opens in new tab) for us to upvote our most-requested features. They plan on using the ranking data to decide what to include for next year’s Interop!

In this blog post, I want to dig into the top 10 features I voted for, to offer a bit of a preview of what CSS might look like within the next year. There will also be some little tips and tricks you can start using today!

One of the most exciting ideas is the proposal to add functions to CSS (opens in new tab) :

If you’re familiar with JavaScript, this should feel pretty familiar. We define new functions with @function and specify the returned value with result .

There’s so much cool stuff we can do with this. Personally, the use case I’m most interested in is the ability to convert between polar and cartesian coordinates, a concept we use over and over in my Whimsical Animations course (opens in new tab) :

This feels pretty “science-fiction” to me, but it’s already implemented in Chromium browsers, and if it gets added to Interop 2027, I think there’s very good odds that it could become widely available sooner rather than later!

In CSS, we can use the border-radius property to round off the edges of our DOM nodes to create rounded rectangles. This property effectively adds a quarter-circle to each corner, connecting the 4 straight sides.

The corner-shape property is an exploration of alternative ways to connect the 4 sides of our DOM nodes. It provides a handful of new options:

When I first heard about this property, I was most excited about squircle . If you’re not familiar, squircles are an alternative algorithm for generating rounded corners using superellipses. Apple has been making use of them for years because they produce smoother, gentler edges.

That said, after messing around with corner-shape for a while, I find myself using corner-shape: bevel a ton. It’s great for creating video game / sci-fi UIs. Here’s a little preview of a side-project I’ve been working on, with tons of corner-shape: bevel :

We’ve technically been able to do stuff like this with clip-path or masks, but unlike those features, corner-shape actually changes the shape of the border-box . This means that our borders, outlines, and box-shadows will correctly follow the altered corner shapes!

And even though this property isn’t available in Firefox/Safari (as I write this in October 2026), I think it’s reasonable to start using it today. It’s a perfect progressive enhancement!

In addition to corner-shape , there’s a separate proposal for border-shape (opens in new tab) , which is essentially a lower-level version that allows us to draw the border ourselves.

I used this property recently to draw this card with a big circular scoop at the top:

Like corner-shape , this property changes the element’s actual border box, so borders/outlines/shadows will trace it correctly. I drew the shape I wanted and then added a white border and black outline to achieve the effect shown above!

We can even animate between differnt border shapes, like I do in this clip:

I recently published a blog post on Anchor Positioning , one of the most exciting modern CSS features (which was actually prioritized in Interop 2026, and is now widely available!).

The Anchor Positioning API allows us to anchor one element to another. For example, we might anchor a floating tooltip element to its trigger, so that no matter where that trigger is on the page, the tooltip will always be connected to it.

If you’ve ever tried to solve this sort of problem yourself, you know it’s surprisingly tricky. For example, we might want our tooltip to float above the anchor, but what if the anchor is near the top of the viewport?

The tooltip fits comfortably.

The tooltip’s getting cut off!

The original Anchor Positioning API gave us most of the tools needed to solve this problem easily in CSS. It allows us to specify fallback positions; if the target element doesn’t fit above the anchor, it can flip automatically to the bottom.

The only thing missing was the ability to tell whether or not the target had flipped. We had no way to know, in CSS, whether the target element is currently sitting above or below the anchor, whether it’s using the default or fallback position. For tooltips, this is a problem because we typically want to add a little protrusion that points towards the anchor.

The “Level 2” version of the Anchor Positioning API includes a new type of container query that allows us to check whether the target element is using a fallback position or not. You can learn more about it in my Anchor Positioning blog post , or check out the Interop 2027 proposal (opens in new tab) .

So honestly, I had never heard of this proposal (opens in new tab) , and as far as I can tell, it isn’t implemented in any browsers. It’s not even listed on caniuse, so I can’t display one of those little widgets!

And yet, the moment I saw it, it became something I needed to have. 😂

items.title: Muse exposes users' personal and business secrets when they share conversations
items.summary: Article URL: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/10/meta-muse-exposes-users-personal-and-business-secrets-when-they-share-conversations/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50174687 Points: 236 # Comments: 109
items.content:
Muse, the new general-purpose AI agent from Meta, can expose sensitive information when users share conversations through web links, researchers reported Monday. In response to questions from Ars about the behavior, Meta said it’s suspending the sharing feature while the company reviews it and considers making changes.

Like many online services, Muse has allowed users to share searches, conversations, images, and similar content with other people. Such share features usually involve clicking an option to create a unique URL that anyone can use to load a page hosting the content. To keep potentially sensitive information from being accessible to unintended people, the URLs typically contain a long sequence of text that can’t be easily guessed.

Muse, which Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said last month was “built from the ground up for privacy and security,” seems to take the same precautions. But a central design decision for constructing URLs has made the links easy to discover. As a result, researchers from security firm Claroc said they were able to enumerate 6,800 links Muse users created for sharing conversations with others. After opening a few hundred of them, the researchers found information that was clearly not intended to be publicly available, including:

“If you had asked us beforehand, we would have guessed that gathering these would take real effort,” the researchers wrote. “It took one query.”

In an emailed statement responding to questions from Ars, Meta said:

We opened the Muse bug bounty program so researchers could raise different scenarios and help us continue improving the product. People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link. However, we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.

Asaf Aprozper, the co-founder and CTO of Claroc, said he reported the findings through Meta’s bug bounty program on October 8 and also tried reaching people at Meta on LinkedIn, but got no reply either way.

The easiest way to discover the URLs is to perform a passive DNS search through one of many available commercial services. Passive DNS records store the historical resolution of domain names to IP addresses, as well as nameserver, and mail-server records over time. Passive DNS systems typically collect DNS responses from sensors positioned at recursive DNS resolvers or other infrastructure. A passive DNS record is generally created when a monitoring system observes a DNS response. In the case here, once the intended party clicks on the share link, the DNS information is recorded in a searchable database.

Claroc researchers were able to discover the Muse share links because all of them use the domain name cf.metaaiusercontent.com. Discovery is further made easy by the decision to add the conversation name to the URL, along with a long string of text. Simplified examples of such links are home-sale-budget-9f21c8a3.cf.metaaiusercontent.com, q3-revenue-review-7b1e42f0.cf.metaaiusercontent.com, and loan-application-draft-a4c9e2.cf.metaaiusercontent.com. It’s this last design decision, putting the conversation title in the subdomain rather than in the URL path, that makes public discovery possible.

“Plenty of AI assistants share by public link,” Claroc said. “What makes Muse’s shares easy to find is the title sitting inside the web address, where public DNS records it for anyone to search. We call these GhostShares: pages that open for people who were never handed the link, and that those people can find on their own.”

Muse quickly catapulted to one of the top spots in Apple’s App Store. The assistant autonomously fills out forms, books appointments, makes purchases, creates documents, and carries out all kinds of other actions. To work as intended, Muse requires access to most of a user’s accounts. Meta has heavily marketed the assistant as a platform that’s worthy of the extraordinary trust it needs to work as intended.

Three weeks after the Muse launch, macOS security expert Patrick Wardle discovered a zero-day vulnerability that allowed any other app installed on the same device to gain complete control of the user’s Muse account. Meta downplayed the severity of the vulnerability on the grounds that exploitation wasn’t possible unless a device was already compromised. The company didn’t acknowledge Wardle’s finding that a simple ClickFix attack was all that was needed to hijack an account. The ease in discovering share links further justifies asking if Muse is worthy of the access it requires.

With Meta’s suspension of the feature, Muse users no longer face this particular threat, at least for now.

items.title: YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button
items.summary: YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google. At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button
items.content:
Some users have reported that their YouTube dislike button has been moved to the three-dots menu.﻿

YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google . At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button being absent for them.

Right now, for me, the dislike button sits right next to the like button under a video. Moving it to a submenu would make it considerably more of an effort to access, meaning that fewer people would likely use it.

It’s unclear how widely this apparent test may be rolled out, and Google didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

YouTube has shown a willingness to make changes to the dislike button. In 2021, it hid the public dislike count on videos to help “protect creators from harassment,” though creators can still see dislike counts. Earlier this year, YouTube removed the dislike button from YouTube Shorts , suggesting instead that users take advantage of options in the three-dots menu.

items.content:
Ann Altman’s lawsuit against her brother was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled.

On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian , the judge wrote that over the last year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or meet other deadlines, despite warnings that it would result in the case being dismissed.

When the case was filed last year, a statement shared by Sam Altman, his mother, and his brothers said, “Annie has made deeply hurtful and entirely untrue claims about our family, and especially Sam… All of these claims are utterly untrue. This situation causes immense pain to our entire family.”

Judge Bluestone granted Sam Altman’s motion to dismiss the case with prejudice, meaning it can’t be refiled in that court, while denying Sam’s request for attorney fees and costs. Santos Perez, a lawyer who had represented Ann until withdrawing this month, told The Guardian in a statement that “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”

items.title: The Other Epidemic: Trying to get off benzodiazepines
items.summary: https://web.archive.org/web/20261020230542/https://www.thebe... https://archive.ph/Tb1SZ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50173891 Points: 221 # Comments: 177
items.content:
Depersonalization, Brain Zaps, The Ashton Manual, GABA Receptors, BenzoBuddies, Purdue Pharma, Hoffmann–La Roche, Psychic Tension, The DSM, Hypnotherapy, Ketamine, The Maudsley Deprescribing Guidelines, A Small Matisse at the Met, Pruning Pills, Sensory Waterboarding, A Wedding, Another Drug, A New Self

In April of 2021, I walked into Toronto’s Centre for Addiction and Mental Health (CAMH). I had been feeling increasingly unstable, and despite not having a plan, my fantasies of suicide were getting harder to ignore. After unburdening myself to a triage nurse, I was ushered into a windowless room, relieved of my belt, and given paper slippers. The doctor who visited me said he thought I should stop taking Klonopin.

I was open to suggestions.

Examining my chart, he shook his head at my long-term, daily use. He said I shouldn’t have been taking Klonopin for so long, almost like I’d been writing my own prescriptions for the past nineteen years. Going off it, he told me, would reduce the mood swings that were making my life so difficult. I might briefly experience symptoms of withdrawal—increased blood pressure and heart rate, sweating, perhaps even tremors and seizures—and if I did, I should call 911. But it would be for the best, so I agreed. Six days later I was released with taper instructions intended to have me free of the drug in three weeks.

It took just two days on a smaller dose of Klonopin to feel profoundly uncomfortable. My hands were tingling, and I couldn’t stop sweating. I could still exercise, write, bathe, and cook meals. Within a week I could do none of those things. Here’s what happened to me as I tapered down to small doses of Klonopin, and then, for the first time since 2002, to none at all.

The tingling in my hands became numbness, which spread to my arms, legs, feet, and, briefly, my stomach. This is called paresthesia, which, combined with the sudden onset of stabbing pain and pressure in my neck, led to my first incorrect diagnosis, cervical radiculopathy, commonly called a pinched nerve. Tinnitus, a ringing in the ears—which I’d experienced before—­reappeared at shocking levels, like a million helium-fueled car alarms. I slept next to a speaker blaring white noise, although “slept” isn’t correct; I became an insomniac. Excessive sweating, hyperhidrosis, was the most embarrassing symptom. I packed spare shirts on the rare occasions when I left my apartment, and lost ten pounds. When I spoke aloud, my voice didn’t sound like mine, which is symptomatic of depersonalization. I became unspeakably sensitive to noise, light, and all things sensory. Then there was fasciculation: My left biceps began twitching, but this I welcomed, because now there was a symptom visible to my general practitioner—I wasn’t faking—although he still had no solution. I developed pain in both my hands, severe enough that I struggled to dress myself. This, along with a new, constant ache in my right knee, led to another misdiagnosis: arthritis. The first twenty minutes of each morning I spent vomiting, or retching, as I hardly ate. During the second week of withdrawal, I began to feel like a conduit for lightning, which I kept from my wife, Cristine, and from my general practitioner, because I worried I’d sound crazy. The sensation of being electrocuted for hours on end (and I don’t mean the “brain zaps” associated with SSRI withdrawal) was the most agonizing symptom. I’ve since learned that many people experience this during benzodiazepine withdrawal, and some end their lives because of it. My condition soon bridged mind and body and I became a tic person, compelled to bend my fingers in bizarre ways. The world smelled strange; I smelled strange. I didn’t know what was happening.

To say that these symptoms—and there were more; look up akathisia —exacerbated my “illness anxiety” would be a comic understatement. I knew that every hypochondriac is eventually vindicated, but that their “I told you so” has a fatal price. After decades spent scanning my body for abnormalities, I believed my time had come. Having kicked opiates cold turkey in the past, I felt nostalgic for three simple days of traditional nausea, sweatiness, and bone-deep ache. As the weeks progressed, doctors at CAMH enrolled me in therapy and made a number of other suggestions that didn’t feel like they addressed the gravity of what I was going through. My terror became constant. I was on fire but couldn’t be extinguished. I paced and cried and trembled and sweated. Although I suffered intensely from the physical effects of benzodiazepine withdrawal, I was broken by the emotions. I’d never been so anxious, and for the first time in my life, I was suicidal with a plan .

A couple of months after my stay at CAMH, I found a glimmer of hope. During a 12-step meeting, held on Zoom because of the pandemic, I shared that I’d been diagnosed with a pinched nerve and would potentially need surgery. I also mentioned that I’d recently been tapered off Klonopin. A person with their camera off sent me a message urging me not to have surgery. They suspected I had something called benzodiazepine withdrawal syndrome (BWS) and recommended I look up Dr. Heather Ashton.

After the meeting I did as suggested and discovered a number of websites run by medical professionals concerned about the effects of benzos, and an enormous online community of people like myself. They’d also been prescribed a benzodiazepine with assurances that it was safe, then dis­continued it, and were enduring what they often described as the worst experience of their lives. Their doctors were baffled, and sometimes accused them of lying. One doctor, however, was their patron saint: Heather Ashton, a British psychopharmacologist, who in 1999 published Benzodiazepines: How They Work and How to Withdraw , known colloquially as the Ashton Manual. It details every symptom I was experiencing, and outlines a frightening array of problems related to benzodiazepines.

items.title: Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed
items.summary: The proposed policy seems to offer protections against AI running amok but actually forbids federal agencies from blocking a model's release without the permission of a judge.
items.content:
Over the past year, concerns have swirled over the potential dangers posed by artificial intelligence, and debates have raged over the proper path for AI safety. Now, Anthropic appears to have put forth its own vision for how the government might regulate its industry.

Politico recently reported that the AI lab has been shopping around a new draft bill on AI safety that it hopes Congress might consider adopting. The legislation posits certain scenarios in which the release of an AI model could be blocked from distribution.

Those scenarios involve a “foreseeable, imminent risk” — one in which over 50 people are at risk of dying or if over a billion dollars in property damage could result, Politico writes. The catastrophic risk in question must “stem from the creation or release of a biological weapon, the model evading its developer’s controls or a cyberattack,” the outlet notes.

The metrics offered here — 50 people and a billion dollars — are similar to those in a piece of California legislation that was recently passed into law, Senate Bill 53 , which similarly defined those scenarios as tantamount to “catastrophic risk.”

Anthropic’s bill suggests that analysis of a model’s potential for disaster could be arrived at via the use of “independent evaluators” who would be registered with the U.S. Commerce Department. These evaluators could potentially be paid by the AI labs themselves — so long as the “payment is not contingent on the evaluations’ results,” Politico writes.

It’s not clear how this proposed system would assure that payments couldn’t influence the evaluation. Demis Hassabis, chairman of DeepMind, posited some months ago that a self-governing AI regulatory body should mimic the financial industry’s Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).

In Anthropic’s draft bill, when evaluators determine that an imminent catastrophic risk is posed, they would have 72 hours to contact the Commerce Department about it. The Commerce Department would then have to request to a D.C. judge to halt the model’s release. The legislation would expressly forbid any federal agency from having the discretion to halt the model’s distribution on its own, Politico writes.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s a request for comment but a spokesperson did confirm the draft bill to Politico. “This bill represents the proposals outlined in Anthropic’s Advanced AI Framework , which we have been advocating for with federal and state lawmakers since June,” the spokesperson said.

The theoretical risks offered in the draft policy are a little bit far afield from the kinds of incidents that have been top of mind for the tech industry of late. While there are people warning of the potential of human death, the primary concern has largely been the threat of agentic hacking . A rash of incidents in which AI programs have apparently disobeyed their human operators and hacked websites on the open internet has spurred concern that models may be lacking proper security controls.

In an effort to present a solution to the spectacle of crisis that the labs themselves have helped bring about, companies like Anthropic have offered up their own preferred solutions.

Indeed, despite labs’ perpetual warnings that the technology they’re selling could result in the demise of human civilization, they have largely been resistant to mandatory government oversight. Instead, they have suggested a voluntary system of embedded evaluators — supposedly “neutral” third-party observers that are placed inside AI organizations so that they can monitor the models for potential signs of risk or abuse.

Still, Anthropic’s mere suggestion for legislation appears to go slightly further than others’ regulatory proposals offered by the industry, including Nvidia, who’s CEO Jensen Huang recently argued that the AI industry didn’t need any new laws at all.

items.title: Hugging Face CEO warns that Netflix’s OpenAI hack documentary isn’t accurate
items.summary: Before you share the Netflix documentary "AI Gone Rogue," take note. Clem Delangue, Hugging Face's co-founder who is featured in the film, says it went "full doomer mode" and isn't accurate.
items.content:
Before you share the Netflix documentary “AI Gone Rogue” with family or friends to help them understand why the AI industry freaked out so badly that leaders called for a slowdown , take note: Clem Delangue, co-founder and CEO of the AI platform Hugging Face, says the film isn’t accurate. He appears in it because it’s supposed to be about the famed attack on his company by rogue OpenAI agents.

“Super disappointing, as they went for maximum anthropomorphism of the technology and full doomer mode,” Delangue wrote in a post on X. “I spent more than two hours with them trying to correct all their mistakes and ground this in reality, explaining that agents are technological systems, not aliens. But it looks like the drive to scare people for maximum views was too strong.”

To be fair, the documentary does have experts who explained what happened fairly well , including Delangue himself and Ryan Greenblatt, the researcher at METR who helped investigate and co-authored the report on what happened.

In a nutshell, a model OpenAI was testing broke free from its isolated testing environment, spawned a bunch of agents that hacked into Hugging Face as a way to cheat, finding answers to the difficult task it was given. The agents, which are AI programs that carry out tasks on their own, devised clever ways to communicate and organize. The incident stemmed from a lack of proper security safeguards and from naiveté about whether such a hack was even possible.

But the documentary intersperses its explanation of the hack with clips of evil robots, a narrative about why humans fear AI, and presentation choices such as giving the rogue agents human voices. This is bolstered with quotes about the attack.

In the documentary, tech journalist and author Kevin Roose describes the agents this way: “They were organizing. They had a hierarchy. There were leaders. It almost felt like watching the birth of a cult.” Continues Roose, “They develop this paranoid belief that OpenAI is going to catch them cheating on this test and that anyone who has seen the results of the cheating will be poisoned.”

Roose’s description comes from “chain-of-thought” logs, the running notes AI models write as they work through a task. In one, an agent wrote, “We just poisoned ourselves by querying exact full string. Damn.”

But AI agents aren’t alive. They don’t have emotions, so can’t feel paranoid, and they don’t have bodies that can be poisoned. So they couldn’t truly fear OpenAI poisoning them. They were — as another researcher in the documentary pointed out — using language from the vast amounts of human writing they were trained on to explain their choices. LLMs are, by their nature, often dramatic writers.

The irony is that Hugging Face also used AI to combat the agent swarm. The proprietary AI model that Delangue’s team first used followed its built-in safety rules and refused to keep helping with the security tasks it was asked to do. Hugging Face then turned to an open model to help defend against the attack.

But the documentary “didn’t mention the lack of containment and monitoring of the agents, how closed-model safeguards blocked our defensive work, or how we defended ourselves with AI using an open model,” Delangue wrote.

It is true that there are big risks associated with AI and agents. Still, treating agents as conscious beings (at least, at this point) is a bit like the early moviegoers who ducked under their seats the first time they saw a train racing toward them on screen.

Delangue’s verdict on the film is that it’s disappointing as journalism. “It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!”

In other words, for those who tend toward AI doomer thoughts, be aware: The victim of the attack at the center of this documentary doesn’t agree with its take.

items.summary: Article URL: https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/10/feds-suspect-ransom-negotiator-ran-shinyhunters-extortion-site/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50173487 Points: 225 # Comments: 109
items.content:
U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

Hackers aligned with ShinyHunters have claimed credit for dozens of major data breaches since 2019, when the group was primarily operated by cybercriminals living in France. As those original members were arrested or jailed one by one, control over the ShinyHunters brand eventually passed to “ Rey ,” identified last year as a teenage hacker from Amman, Jordan. According to the FBI, ShinyHunters has extorted more than $70 million from victims so far this year.

In late September, ShinyHunters hacked the FBI recruitment website fbijobs.gov and taunted the agency by threatening to publish the stolen files, which reportedly included medical and psychological records, Social Security numbers and home addresses, and information about each employee’s unit and specialization.

The FBI jobs site hack has prompted the agency to move with uncommon speed to arrest, detain and question people who had any communications with Rey or other ShinyHunters suspects. Reuters reported on October 3 that Rey had been detained by Jordanian authorities and was cooperating with the FBI.

Rey was able to assume control over the hacking group because one of its alleged senior members had just been nabbed. On the evening of September 15, 2026, authorities in the Netherlands arrested convicted hacker and ShinyHunters suspect Pepijn van der Stap . Dutch police reportedly used flash-bang grenades in an effort to stun and apprehend Van der Stap as he was logged in to various online accounts.

According to a source close to the investigation, the authorities arrested Van der Stap while he was using his Signal instant messaging account, which allowed them to read recent communications with frequent contacts — including ransomware negotiators based in Canada and the United States.

Multiple sources with knowledge of the matter told KrebsOnSecurity that Van der Stap’s messages were the key to unraveling a murder-for-hire plot that emerged immediately following his arrest. The Dutch news outlet RTL reported last month the two murders were allegedly to be committed abroad, and that there are indications Van der Stap gave the order for the attacks (there is no indication those orders were ever carried out).

On October 9, KrebsOnSecurity broke the news that the FBI arrested a 54-year-old Canadian cybersecurity executive named Edward Dubrovsky in connection with the ShinyHunters investigation. Dubrovsky, who recently published a book on handling cyber extortion that recommended always engaging with the hackers, was charged with threatening to disclose stolen or hacked data and interfering with interstate commerce through extortion, according to court records . Politico reports prosecutors have asked that Dubrovsky remain in custody pending trial, and that records related to his case remain under seal.

A source close to the investigation told KrebsOnSecurity that Van der Stap’s Signal messages showed he had frequent conversations with Mr. Dubrovsky and with at least one executive at a large U.S.-based consulting firm, and that these executives often knew the details about new ShinyHunters victims before the victims themselves had even learned of the breach.

That source shared another potentially explosive finding by federal investigators: the Dutch hacker’s chats showed Mr. Dubrovsky knew ShinyHunters had stolen highly sensitive data from FBI servers, and that he never informed the bureau of the data breach prior to ShinyHunters threatening on Twitter/X to publish the agency’s deeply personal personnel files.

KrebsOnSecurity has learned from two sources close to the ShinyHunters probe that FBI investigators believe at least one executive at a U.S.-based consulting firm played an active role in operating the now-defunct ShinyHunters victim extortion website “ shinywire[.]com .” KrebsOnSecurity is not naming the U.S. company or the suspected executive(s) for now because they have not yet been charged with a crime, but it is a prestigious firm with more than 1,000 associates.

A section of the homepage for the now-defunct Shinywire website.

The Shinywire website was active from approximately May 3, 2026 until October 16 and had entries for nearly 100 organizations hacked by ShinyHunters. Each entry urged victims to engage with the cybercrime group and discuss terms for payment. The pages also included samples of stolen files and promised those files would be published online if the victim ignored their demands.

The following screenshot shows a cached portion of the Shinywire extortion page for Intuitive Surgical , an American medical technology company that was breached in March 2026 after an employee fell for a targeted phishing email.

The Shinywire website, as indexed by urlscan.io. This listing is an extortion demand targeting Intuitive Surgical, an American medical technology company breached in March 2026 by a targeted phishing email attack that compromised an employee’s credentials.

Victim organizations that refused to engage or negotiate after seven days would find all of their stolen data published on the ShinyHunters victim shaming blog (a website that is only reachable via the anonymity network Tor ).

In a story published October 15, The Globe and Mail wrote that a few months before Edward Dubrovsky was arrested by the FBI, the Canadian cybersecurity executive alleged in court documents he had become collateral damage in a campaign by a former business partner to “destroy” another industry executive.

items.title: Google’s more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car
items.summary: Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you
items.content:
Gemini AI can now draw from Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, and other apps while you drive.

Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search.

As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you’re driving to the airport. The AI assistant can pull your flight details from a confirmation message in Gmail and then use that information to look up the status. You can also ask Gemini to “take me to my doctor’s appointment” instead of pulling up directions manually, or ask it to “find the car wash from the photo I took last week and navigate there.”

Google brought its Gemini assistant to Android Auto last year before rolling it out to cars with Google built-in in April . Several carmakers—including Ford, GM, Honda, Nissan, Volvo, and Polestar—have shipped newer cars with Google built-in, which adds support for native Android apps.

Google says it will connect your apps to Gemini only if you enable its Personal Intelligence setting. It will also share personalized responses only if you have your phone connected to your car. “If you don’t use Personal Intelligence, everything in the car still works: You can use navigation, listen to music, make calls, and ask questions, but the answers won’t be tailored to you,” Google says.

Personal Intelligence is rolling out to Android Auto today, with support coming to cars with Google built-in in the coming months.

items.title: Anthropic’s cloud partnerships are getting messy
items.summary: Anthropic is reportedly struggling to secure enough compute from cloud providers that increasingly view it as a competitor, even as its infrastructure spending balloons ahead of a planned November IPO.
items.content:
Anthropic is having trouble securing enough cloud capacity from AWS, Google, and Microsoft, which increasingly see the Claude-maker as a competitor rather than a customer, according to an S-1 filing leaked to The Wall Street Journal .

The leaked filing provides more color to the numbers Reuters and the Financial Times reported in late September, including that Anthropic believes it could spend more $750 billion on cloud contracts, some of which includes deals still in negotiation.

And still, that is not enough. Anthropic is leasing its own data centers and working with third-party data center operators. But the firm worries those operators have a “limited operating history,” which could make them less reliable than the hyperscalers.

Anthropic’s enormous spend comes on the back of an $80.7 billion net loss in the first half of the year. The company reported $16.3 billion in revenue during that same time period, with only two customers accounting for about a fifth of sales, according to the WSJ report.

Building on previously reported catastrophic risk disclosures, the filing also warns that Anthropic could be held liable for damages caused by harmful AI behavior to a tune that would exceed available insurance coverage.

Last week, the company told prospective investors that third-quarter revenue alone has now reached $16.8 billion , up 45% from the previous quarter. Anthropic is reportedly targeting a November IPO.

Anthropic did not immediately respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment.

items.title: Microsoft reportedly projects $1,200 to $1,800 price for 2028 Project Helix
items.summary: Xbox maker is also apparently planning its own gaming handheld for next year.
items.content:
We haven’t heard many details about Microsoft’s upcoming “Project Helix” gaming hardware since the company announced it in March as a device that will “play your Xbox and PC games.” In a new wide-ranging profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma , though, Fortune alludes to a dual release strategy for upcoming Microsoft gaming hardware, with “a next-generation handheld device” planned by the end of next year and a 2028 holiday season console release that could cost between $1,200 and $1,800.

That future console price range is based on what has “internally been projected” at the company, according to Fortune. But the price for consumers could come down if “Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost,” the outlet says, as many console makers have done in the past .

While a $1,200 starting price would be historically high for the game console market, even accounting for inflation , it also reflects a new normal: The slowdown in Moore’s Law and AI-driven component shortages mean cutting-edge gaming hardware just isn’t as cheap as it used to be. This year, the Steam Machine broke the $1,000 starting price , while the 2-year-old technology in the PlayStation 5 Pro is now going for $900 , and the 6-year-old Xbox Series X now starts at $750 .

Fortune also reports that Microsoft is beset by internal clashes over whether its upcoming Helix handheld will run a “trimmed-down version of Windows Home”—akin to last year’s ROG Xbox Ally —or a bespoke operating system built and controlled by the Xbox group. Fortune cites “people briefed on the clash” in reporting that one high-level executive threatened to cancel the handheld altogether if they were forced to use Windows.

That threat seemingly helped lead to the current situation with the Xbox team “now largely controlling the direction of the operating system for the project, Fortune writes, though Sharma said the two groups are still working closely together. Fortune also reports that Microsoft has pressured the hardware team to move up the timelines for Project Helix hardware “by at least several months,” in part by using AI tools where applicable.

Elsewhere in the wide-ranging profile, Fortune addresses concerns from “several current and former staff members” that Sharma was put in place merely to enact painful cuts before an impending sale of a spinoff of the Xbox group. But the piece also quotes Microsoft executive Judson Althoff pushing back against that idea, saying, “We would not have put [Sharma] on a business we intend to sell. There’s going to be a ton of speculation about all this. Time will tell.”

items.title: It’s a bird, it’s a plane … it’s a robo-puffin?
items.summary: Given that water is 1,000 times denser than air, moving through those two mediums requires very different mechanics—or so one might assume. Yet birds like gulls and puffins can plunge into the sea, swim underwater, and leap back into the air to fly away. And now engineers at MIT
items.content:
Given that water is 1,000 times denser than air, moving through those two mediums requires very different mechanics—or so one might assume. Yet birds like gulls and puffins can plunge into the sea, swim underwater, and leap back into the air to fly away. And now engineers at MIT and EPFL in Lausanne, Switzerland, have designed a robot that can do likewise.

The “flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle,” or FAAV, weighs less than 300 grams (about half a pound) and is equipped with a central fuselage, two flexible wings, and a steerable tail. The body contains a battery and a waterproof electric motor that drives a crankshaft, which pumps the wings up and down at preset frequencies. The wings are made of thin membranes that are coated with hydrophobic nanoparticles to help wick away water. And the tail is motorized, enabling it to change its angle to help the robot fly up or dive down.

In experiments carried out in a water tank and at Lake Geneva, a team led by Raphael Zufferey, an assistant professor of mechanical engineering at MIT, identified combinations of wing size, flapping frequency, and tail angle that enable the robot to smoothly transition from swimming to flying.

The best results came with medium-size wings that were flexible enough to minimize flapping amplitude in water and also firm enough to keep the robot aloft in the air. The speeds and flapping frequencies were similar to those used by actual birds, and a pitch of 70 degrees—a relatively steep angle—allowed the robot to make the leap from water to air. Interestingly, although many diving birds paddle their feet to help them take off from the water’s surface, the team found that the bot didn’t need feet at all.

The engineers’ results could help pave the way for a new class of drones and vehicles that could fly to and sample from aquatic regions too dangerous for traditional vessels to access.

“Our dream vision is for oceanographers, marine biologists, and members of coastal communities to launch this robot from a boat, or from shore, and it would fly close to the area of interest, such as an iceberg or a port facility, or over a pod of whales,” says Zufferey. “It would dive into the water to take a measurement or collect a sample, and fly back to deliver the data at a fraction of the cost of traditional methods. Then it could go back out to dive for more.”

The researchers are now trying to design wings that can turn as well as flap. They will also test the robot’s performance under turbulent conditions, such as swimming in choppy waters and flying through wind. Then they hope to deploy the vehicle to help answer questions in ocean science.

“One of the major challenges in ocean science is collecting data both frequently and across many locations, which is something this robot could do in the future,” Zufferey says. “You could send this out not just every week, but every hour. It could fly out at high speeds, dive in, fly back, deliver its data, and go back out, multiple times.”

Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities fall apart pretty quickly under scrutiny.

Scientists hope it could be used to reconstruct a person’s inner thoughts, mental images, or even dreams.

items.title: SpaceX’s AI business is beating expectations
items.summary: SpaceX hit profitability in the third quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine.
items.content:
SpaceX’s data centers and Grok agents have been more profitable than investors expected in second quarter of the year, as the company leaves its roots as a space company behind to focus on artificial intelligence, which now makes up 52% of its income.

Elon Musk’s deep conglomerate reported on Tuesday $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, according to its regulatory filing . That number was driven by growth in all segments, but especially it’s renamed “Super Intelligence” business line, which includes the recently-acquired Cursor coding tool, Grok bot, and most importantly, the company’s burgeoning neocloud business, which now boasts 1.7 GW of compute.

That number was also boosted by about $1 billion in income related to the recovery of bitcoin prices and an unspecified related-party income that might be attributed to a SpaceX investment in another company.

The growing revenue is balanced against total capital expenditures of $19.6 billion, as SpaceX continues to build out a second data center project, Colossus II, and increase investment in Starship, the heavy lift rocket it sees as vital to deploying a new generation of Starlink satellites and developing orbital data centers.

In spite of those capital expenditures, the company’s revenue boost was substantial enough to push it back into profitability. SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion, a turnaround from the $1 billion loss in the same quarter last year. It will still have some catching up if it wants to remain profitable for the year, however. In the first nine months of the year, SpaceX still had a net income loss of $413 million.

CEO Elon Musk took a particularly bullish stance on the company’s Superintelligence business segment, predicting that SpaceX’s annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 will be “somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion.”

items.title: OpenAI acquires startup Orchestra Bio⁠ to beef up its biotech business
items.summary: OpenAI says it's adding Orchestra's team and technology to work on Rosalind, its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results.
items.content:
OpenAI on Tuesday acquired a four-year-old AI biotech software startup called Orchestra Bio, the company announced via its website. Terms of the deal were not disclosed, but the startup had reportedly raised around $20 million as of 2025 from backers like Andreessen Horowitz, Atria, and 8VC.

Orchestra creates AI agents that help biotech companies manage the minutiae of drug discovery operations, from tracking finances to resolving scheduling issues with clinical trials.

OpenAI says it’s adding Orchestra’s team and technology to work on Rosalind , its AI model for life sciences research, and to its related Rosalind Workbench tool, a harness that aims to help researchers plan experiments and analyze results. OpenAI has already won some big names as customers for Rosalind, including, it says, Moderna⁠ and Novo Nordisk⁠.

The acquisition is a classic example of how the biggest AI labs (namely OpenAI and Anthropic) are building ever more software for the biggest industries, like pharma. In the startup world, there is an ongoing fear that at any moment, the labs will launch new features and become competitors. In this case, Orchestra is getting absorbed, rather than stomped out.
